reason: Judged on title alone (no abstract): describes switching from culture to the Cepheid Carba-R multiplex nucleic acid amplification test for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae in screening samples, so it evaluates the asked-about assay class in a workflow-transition context.

title: Evaluation of three commercial assays for rapid detection of genes encoding clinically relevant carbapenemases in cultured bacteria
reason: Assesses three commercial multiplex molecular assays (Check-Direct CPE, eazyplex SuperBug complete A, Xpert Carba-R) for KPC, NDM, VIM, OXA-48-like and IMP genes on 450 isolates, 438 of them Enterobacteriaceae.

title: Carbapenem Resistance: A Review
reason: General review of carbapenem resistance epidemiology and mechanisms in Gram-negative pathogens; background context only, with no multiplex gene detection assay presented.

title: Multiplex detection of the big five carbapenemase genes using solid-phase recombinase polymerase amplification
reason: Develops solid-phase multiplex recombinase polymerase amplification detecting all five 'big five' carbapenemase gene sequences with femtomolar limits in a spatially separated multiplex format: a multiplex amplification assay for the common carbapenemase genes.

title: Multiplex Real-Time PCR Assay for Six Major Carbapenemase Genes
reason: Multiplex real-time PCR in two sets covering six major carbapenemase genes (blaNDM, blaKPC, blaIMP, blaGES, blaOXA-48, blaVIM), applied to reference and clinical CPE isolates including six carrying both NDM and OXA-48-like.

title: Occurrence and characteristics of extended spectrum beta-lactamases-producing Enterobacteriaceae from foods of animal origin
reason: Occurrence survey of ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae in chicken meat, milk and cheese with blaTEM, blaCTX-M and blaSHV frequencies; no carbapenemase genes and no clinical isolates, so a different subject entirely.

title: Primer Evaluation for PCR and its Application for Detection of Carbapenemases in Enterobacteriaceae
reason: Designs and evaluates primers for multiplex PCR sets giving simultaneous identification of class A, B and D carbapenem-hydrolysing beta-lactamases (11 genes) in Enterobacteriaceae, tested on reference strains and nine clinical isolates.

title: Rapid detection of NDM, KPC and OXA-48 carbapenemases directly from positive blood cultures using a new multiplex immunochromatographic assay.
reason: New multiplex immunochromatographic test (RESIST-3 O.K.N.) detecting NDM, KPC and OXA-48-like directly from positive blood cultures of 170 Enterobacteriaceae isolates; simultaneous detection of common carbapenemases but antigen-based, not amplification.

title: Multiplex PCR Detection of Common Carbapenemase Genes and Identification of Clinically Relevant Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae Complex
reason: Multiplex PCR detecting […] species identification, correctly typed across 840 clinical Enterobacterales including E. coli and the K. pneumoniae complex.

title: Multiplex Real-Time PCR for Detection of an Epidemic KPC-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST258 Clone
reason: Multiplex real-time PCR in a single reaction on 75 K. pneumoniae isolates, but it pairs blaKPC with identification of the epidemic ST258 clone, so the aim is clone surveillance rather than simultaneous detection of the common carbapenemase gene families.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Real-Time PCR Assay for Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenemase Genes
reason: Real-time TaqMan PCR detecting blaKPC (with restriction digestion to separate KPC-1/-2/-3) in clinical K. pneumoniae and K. oxytoca; amplification-based carbapenemase gene detection in enteric isolates but a single-target, not multiplex, assay.

title: Carbapenem-non-susceptible Enterobacteriaceae in Europe: conclusions from a meeting of national experts
reason: Conclusions of a 31-country expert consultation on carbapenem-non-susceptible Enterobacteriaceae in Europe, indexing diagnostic gaps and staging spread; policy and epidemiology context rather than a multiplex assay.

title: Prevalence and Fate of Carbapenemase Genes in a Wastewater Treatment Plant in Northern China
reason: Quantifies five carbapenemase genes by real-time qPCR through a wastewater treatment plant and isolates KPC-2 producers; the same technique and gene targets applied to an environmental fate question, not clinical isolate detection.

title: Rapid detection of carbapenemase genes by multiplex real-time PCR
reason: Single multiplex real-time PCR distinguishing six carbapenemase gene types (KPC, GES, NDM, IMP, VIM, OXA-48) by melting temperature, validated on 58 isolates including 21 Enterobacteriaceae, in one 3 h run.

title: Development of a Two Triplex Real-Time Polymerase Chain Reaction for Rapid Detection of Six Carbapenemase Genes in Enterobacteriaceae
journal: Osong Public Health and Research Perspectives
reason: Two triplex TaqMan real-time PCRs for the six clinically prevalent carbapenemase genes (KPC, NDM, OXA, IMP, VIM, GES) validated by direct colony testing on a blinded panel of 310 Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

title: Evaluation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay for detection of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in cultures
reason: Judged on title alone (no abstract): evaluates a loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay for detecting carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in cultures, so an amplification assay on enteric cultures, but the title does not indicate multiplexed detection of the common carbapenemase gene panel.

title: Single-Tube Multiplex Polymerase Chain Reaction for the Detection of Genes Encoding Enterobacteriaceae Carbapenemase
reason: Single-tube multiplex PCR amplifying six Enterobacteriaceae carbapenemase genes (blaKPC, blaIMP, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaOXA-48-like, blaGES) with 100% sensitivity and specificity across 51 carbapenemase-positive and 91 negative clinical isolates.

title: Rapid Detection of KPC, NDM, and OXA-48-Like Carbapenemases by Real-Time PCR from Rectal Swab Surveillance Samples
reason: Multiplex real-time TaqMan PCR detecting all described KPC, NDM and OXA-48-like carbapenemases from bacterial culture or enrichment broth lysates of rectal swab surveillance samples: simultaneous amplification detection of common carbapenemase genes.

title: Prospective evaluation of the OKN K-SeT assay, a new multiplex immunochromatographic test for the rapid detection of OXA-48-like, KPC and NDM carbapenemases
reason: Prospective evaluation of the OKN K-SeT multiplex lateral flow assay for OXA-48-like, KPC and NDM producers from colonies; addresses the same rapid simultaneous detection need but explicitly positions itself as an alternative to molecular assays.

title: Multiplex Immunochromatographic Detection of OXA-48, KPC, and NDM Carbapenemases: Impact of Inoculum, Antibiotics, and Agar.
reason: Assesses the multiplex Resist-3 O.K.N. immunochromatographic test for OXA-48-like, KPC and NDM on 63 carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, focusing on inoculum, carbapenem disks and zinc-supplemented agar; enzyme detection, not gene amplification.

title: Evaluation of the RESIST-4 K-SeT assay, a multiplex immunochromatographic assay for the rapid detection of OXA-48-like, KPC, VIM and NDM carbapenemases.
reason: Evaluation of the RESIST-4 K-SeT multiplex immunochromatographic assay for OXA-48-like, KPC, VIM and NDM across 479 Enterobacteriaceae and non-fermenter isolates; simultaneous detection of the common carbapenemases but by lateral flow rather than multiplex amplification.

title: Simultaneous and Visual Detection of KPC and NDM Carbapenemase-Encoding Genes Using Asymmetric PCR and Multiplex Lateral Flow Strip.
journal: Journal of Analytical Methods in Chemistry
reason: Asymmetric PCR combined with a multiplex lateral flow strip for simultaneous detection of the blaKPC-2 and blaNDM-1 carbapenemase-encoding genes, validated by genotyping clinical carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates against qPCR and sequencing.

title: Nucleic acid detection with CRISPR-Cas13a/C2c2
reason: Describes the Cas13a-based SHERLOCK nucleic acid detection platform combining isothermal amplification with collateral RNase activity, demonstrated on Zika, Dengue, human genotyping and tumour DNA; methodological background with no carbapenemase gene targets.

title: Activity of ceftazidime/avibactam against problem Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the UK, 2015–16
reason: Reports ceftazidime/avibactam susceptibility rates against referred Enterobacteriaceae and P. aeruginosa; carbapenemase genes were only sought by PCR incidentally, so it answers a therapy-spectrum question about the same organisms, not a detection assay question.

title: Multiplex PCR amplification assay for the detection of bla SHV, bla TEM and bla CTX‐M genes in Enterobacteriaceae
reason: Multiplex PCR amplification assay discriminating blaSHV, blaTEM and blaCTX-M amplicons in clinical Enterobacteriaceae isolates: the same assay format and setting applied to the closely related ESBL gene families rather than carbapenem-hydrolysing enzymes.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Extended-spectrum Beta-lactamase Genes in Escherichia coli Isolates Using Multiplex PCR Technique
journal: Jentashapir Journal of Cellular and Molecular Biology
reason: Multiplex PCR designed to detect TEM, AmpC and KPC simultaneously in 50 clinical E. coli isolates; includes one carbapenemase target within an otherwise ESBL-focused resistance profiling panel.

title: Development of a set of multiplex PCR assays for the detection of genes encoding important β-lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae
reason: Develops a set of six multiplex PCRs plus one simplex PCR covering OXA-1-like, ESBL, plasmid AmpC and class A, B and D carbapenemase genes in Enterobacteriaceae, but the 31 clinical isolates evaluated yielded only ESBL and AmpC producers, so carbapenemase detection is one component rather than the reported finding.

title: The Role and Limitations of Large Language Models Such as ChatGPT in Clinical Settings and Medical Journalism
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Covers roles and limitations of ChatGPT in clinical settings and medical journalism, which is background on clinical LLM risk but says nothing about distributed ledgers, audit trails or scaled individualised care governance.

title: Leveraging ChatGPT to Democratize and Decolonize Global Surgery: Large Language Models for Small Healthcare Budgets
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title frames LLMs as an equity/cost tool for global surgery in low-budget systems, same general area of clinical LLM use but no ledger, provenance or auditing mechanism.

title: Towards convergence of AI and blockchain for personalized medicine in pharmacogenomics
reason: Abstract describes blockchain smart-contract commitment of model inputs and predictions with on-chain audit logs and tamper detection for personalised pharmacogenomic medicine. Same ledger-based auditing of AI outputs in individualised care, but the audited model is a Random Forest regressor rather than a generative language model, so it answers the question for a closely related system.

title: Generative AI could revolutionize health care — but not if control is ceded to big tech
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Concerns who controls generative AI in health care (big tech vs. public interest), a governance-adjacent commentary with no distributed ledger, audit architecture or deployment auditing mechanism.

title: GPT-4 in a Cancer Center — Institute-Wide Deployment Challenges and Lessons Learned
reason: Abstract reports institute-wide GPT-4 rollout at a cancer center with policy guardrails and a compliant, auditable, secure environment, but the stated mechanisms are governance process and secure IT, not distributed ledgers, and it explicitly excludes use in direct clinical care, so it is context on scaled deployment rather than an answer.

title: Large Language Models Are Poor Clinical Decision-Makers: A Comprehensive Benchmark
reason: Abstract field contains only an author list and venue citation; title indicates a benchmark showing LLMs are poor clinical decision-makers. Establishes the failure modes that motivate oversight but offers no ledger, audit or provenance component.

title: ChainTrust-LLM: Secure and Auditable Hallucination Mitigation in Medical LLMs Using Blockchain and Expert Feedback
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title states secure and auditable hallucination mitigation in medical LLMs using blockchain and expert feedback, which is precisely a distributed ledger used to constrain and audit a clinical generative model.

title: Large Language Models in Healthcare: An Urgent Call for Ongoing, Rigorous Validation
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Calls for ongoing rigorous validation of healthcare LLMs, an oversight argument in the same subject area but without any distributed ledger or tamper-evident audit proposal.

title: Prompt Ledger: AI Governance Infrastructure for Institutional Deployment
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
reason: Abstract presents an audit-first governance layer that enforces policy before execution and creates immutable audit trails and provenance for institutional LLM deployment at scale, which answers the constrain-and-audit half of the question, but the setting is generic enterprise rather than individualised clinical care and the ledger is a proxy audit sidecar rather than a distributed ledger.

title: Audit Trails for Accountability in Large Language Models
reason: Abstract proposes tamper-evident, append-only audit trails linking technical provenance and governance records for LLM lifecycles, naming healthcare among the consequential domains. Supplies a real part of the answer on auditing deployed LLMs, though it is not distributed-ledger-based and not specific to individualised clinical care.

title: Simulated misuse of large language models and clinical credit systems
reason: Abstract simulates biased LLM resource allocation and AI-driven clinical credit systems. It motivates why deployed clinical LLMs need external constraint but studies the misuse risk itself, with no ledger, audit trail or oversight architecture.

title: Cryptographically Verifiable Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Tripartite Architecture For Decentralized Provenance, Compute-to-Data Privacy, And Automated Fact-Checking
reason: Abstract builds a verifiable RAG stack with decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials and on-chain mapping to create immutable audit trails plus an automated verifier agent auditing LLM output against anchored evidence. That is distributed-ledger constraint and audit of a generative model, but for generic RAG rather than individualised clinical care.

title: Testing and Evaluation of Generative Large Language Models in Electronic Health Record Applications: A Systematic Review
reason: Abstract is a PRISMA systematic review of evaluation metrics for generative LLMs on EHR data across specialties and tasks. Concerns performance evaluation frameworks, not ledger-based provenance, tamper-evident logging or deployment-time constraint.

title: Accountable Clinical AI Requires More Than Accuracy
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
reason: Abstract argues accountability rather than accuracy gates clinical LLM deployment and explicitly proposes distributed ledger and related audit technologies […], matching the question directly.

title: Safe Implementation of Large Language Models in Clinical Care Requires Acknowledgment of Their Limitations and Strong Regulation to Prevent Misuse
reason: Truncated abstract and title argue that safe clinical LLM implementation needs acknowledgment of limitations and strong regulation against misuse. Addresses constraint only as policy and regulation, with no distributed ledger or technical audit mechanism.

title: From text to treatment: the crucial role of validation for generative large language models in health care
reason: Abstract stresses thorough validation of generative LLMs before health-care use because hallucinations harm patients. Same problem framing as the question's motivation, but validation is offered instead of ledger-based auditing or provenance.

title: Taming Unleashed Large Language Models With Blockchain for Massive Personalized Reliable Healthcare.
journal: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
reason: Abstract describes CHATCBD using blockchain to decentralize external regulation of LLM personalised diagnoses, with a blockchain-based audit framework and routing management for massive personalised reliable healthcare, which is exactly distributed-ledger constraint and audit of clinical generative models at scale.

title: Publicly Shareable Clinical Large Language Model Built on Synthetic Clinical Notes
reason: Abstract field holds only an author list and venue; the title concerns constructing a shareable clinical LLM from synthetic clinical notes. Same organism of interest (clinical LLMs) but the question of model building and data sharing, not ledger auditing or oversight.

title: How large language models including generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) 3 and 4 will impact medicine and surgery
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. A forward-looking commentary on how GPT-3 and GPT-4 will affect medicine and surgery, general clinical LLM context with no audit, provenance or distributed ledger content.

title: Blockchain Audit Trails Resolve the Electronic Health Record Traceability Problem Created by Generative AI
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
reason: Abstract specifies append-only, cryptographically chained blockchain audit logging capturing model identity, prompt hash, output fingerprint and timestamp for LLM-generated clinical documentation, proposed as a standard condition of institutional LLM deployment, directly answering the question.

title: Subcellular distribution of p21 and PCNA in normal and repair-deficient cells following DNA damage
reason: Title only (no abstract): subcellular distribution of PCNA and p21 is the right kind of measurement, but the trigger studied is DNA damage in repair-deficient cells, not preparation for cell cycle exit.

title: Transdifferentiation of Epithelial Glomerular Cells
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
reason: Subject is epithelial-to-mesenchymal transdifferentiation of podocytes in glomerular disease; PCNA appears only as a proliferation stain, with nothing on nuclear positioning of replication machinery.

title: Functional Disruption of IQGAP1 by Truncated PALB2 in Two Cases of Breast Cancer: Implications for Proliferation and Invasion
reason: IQGAP1 localisation in PALB2-truncated breast carcinoma; PCNA is used only as an S-phase co-stain, and the reorganisation described is cytoskeletal, not nuclear replication machinery.

title: PCNA is ubiquitinated by RNF8
reason: Concerns a replication machinery component (PCNA) but the question addressed is RNF8-mediated mono- and polyubiquitination in DNA damage tolerance, with no nuclear spatial distribution or cycle exit.

title: Poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation reactions in the regulation of nuclear functions
reason: Review of poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation as a post-translational modification in DNA repair and nucleic acid metabolism; no treatment of replication foci position or quiescence entry.

title: Replication factories and nuclear bodies: the ultrastructural characterization of replication sites during the cell cycle
reason: Ultrastructural mapping of replication factories in HeLa nuclei shows when factories form, how their size and number change through S phase, and their positioning on the nucleoskeleton and beneath the lamina, a real part of the spatial-organisation answer, but for cycling cells rather than cells leaving the cycle.

title: Nuclear envelope remodelling during mitosis
reason: Reviews nuclear envelope breakdown and reformation strategies during mitosis; concerns the envelope in division, not replication machinery redistribution before cycle exit.

title: Nuclear reorganization of mammalian DNA synthesis prior to cell cycle exit.
reason: Exactly the question asked: in primary mammalian cells, perinucleolar lamin A/C-associated replication foci persist through S phase and PCNA and pol delta stay concentrated there as cells approach exit by contact inhibition, serum starvation or senescence, with loci redirected to the nucleolus.

title: The nuclear envelope at a glance
reason: Overview of inner and outer nuclear membrane proteins and nuclear pore complexes; membrane biology rather than nuclear placement of the replication apparatus.

title: Nuclear Lamins
journal: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
reason: Lamin review that notes lamin roles in DNA replication and in spatial chromosome organisation, so useful background for perinucleolar lamin-associated foci, but it does not examine replication machinery relocation at cycle exit.

title: A transient pool of nuclear F-actin at mitotic exit controls chromatin organization
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): a transient nuclear F-actin pool at mitotic exit controlling chromatin organisation concerns mitosis-to-interphase transition, not replication machinery or exit from the division cycle.

title: Selective Nuclear Pore Complex Removal Drives Nuclear Envelope Division in Fission Yeast
reason: Fission yeast nuclear pore removal and nuclear envelope fission during closed mitosis; a different organism and a different process from mammalian replication foci reorganisation.

title: PCNA binding proteins.
reason: Review of PCNA partner proteins and their roles in replication, repair and cell cycle regulation; the reorganisation discussed is of replicated DNA at forks, not of machinery position in the nucleus.

title: PCNA Loaders and Unloaders—One Ring That Rules Them All
reason: Covers PCNA loader and unloader complexes controlling clamp recruitment and turnover on chromatin, background on the machinery itself with no nuclear spatial mapping or cycle exit condition.

title: Dynamic positioning of the fission yeast cell division plane
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Positioning of the cytokinetic division plane by mid1p in Schizosaccharomyces pombe; shares only the word positioning with the question and involves no replication proteins.

title: Nuclear organisation and replication timing are coupled through RIF1–PP1 interaction
reason: Links nuclear architecture to the replication-timing programme via RIF1-PP1, which is adjacent background, but the readout is timing rather than where replication machinery sits, and cycle exit is not studied.

title: A somatic cell-derived system for studying both early and late mitotic events in vitro
reason: Cell-free chicken extract system for mitotic nuclear envelope breakdown, lamina depolymerisation and reassembly; a mitotic disassembly assay, not replication machinery localisation.

title: Transcription-coupled structural dynamics of topologically associating domains regulate replication origin efficiency.
reason: STORM imaging shows high-efficiency origins relocating to the TAD periphery before S phase and PCNA forming immobile clusters around TADs at G1/S, so it supplies real evidence on spatial repositioning of replication machinery in human nuclei, although the paper's own question is origin efficiency, not cycle exit.

title: Control of M-G1 phase-specific expression in fission yeast
reason: Transcriptional control of M-G1 phase-specific gene expression in fission yeast; a transcription programme in yeast rather than nuclear positioning of mammalian replication machinery.

title: Nuclear reorganization of DNA mismatch repair proteins in response to DNA damage.
reason: Does track nuclear reorganisation of hMSH2, hMLH1 and PCNA on chromatin in synchronised HeLa cells, but the reorganisation is a response to alkylating DNA damage and G2 arrest, not preparation to leave the cycle.

title: The highly conserved nuclear lamin Ig-fold binds to PCNA: its role in DNA replication
reason: Shows the lamin Ig-fold binds PCNA and that lamins, PCNA and chromatin associate in situ, relevant mechanistic background for lamin-associated replication sites, but the paper's subject is the Ig-fold mutation and replication activity, not spatial reorganisation at cycle exit.

title: Discrimination of cell cycle phases in PCNA-immunolabeled cells
reason: Uses characteristic PCNA distribution patterns to classify cell cycle phases; the paper's contribution is an image-analysis and classification pipeline rather than findings about machinery redistribution before quiescence.

title: Role of cki-2 during development in C. elegans
reason: Function of the CDK inhibitor cki-2 in C. elegans germline centriole elimination and early embryonic divisions; different organism and a different cell cycle question entirely.

title: Dynamics of DNA Replication Factories in Living Cells
reason: GFP-PCNA live-cell imaging of replication foci showing […] change pattern by gradual assembly and disassembly through S phase, a substantial part of the spatial-dynamics answer without the cycle-exit condition.

title: A short G1 phase imposes constitutive replication stress and fork remodelling in mouse embryonic stem cells
reason: Concerns constitutive replication stress, fork slowing and fork reversal in mouse ESCs and its loss at differentiation onset; mammalian replication and cell cycle background, but no nuclear spatial mapping of the machinery.

title: Re-modelling of nuclear architecture in quiescent and senescent human fibroblasts
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): re-modelling of nuclear architecture in quiescent and senescent human fibroblasts covers exactly the exit states in question and the nuclear reorganisation accompanying them, though the title does not specify replication machinery.

title: DNA Polymerase Clamp Shows Little Turnover at Established Replication Sites but Sequential De Novo Assembly at Adjacent Origin Clusters
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): little turnover of the polymerase clamp at established replication sites versus sequential de novo assembly at adjacent origin clusters is directly about how replication machinery is distributed and rebuilt at nuclear sites, but says nothing about cycle exit.

title: Replication protein A dynamically re-organizes on primer/template junctions to permit DNA polymerase δ holoenzyme assembly and initiation of DNA synthesis.
reason: In vitro FRET study of RPA re-organising on primer/template junctions during pol delta holoenzyme assembly; the reorganisation is molecular on naked DNA, not spatial within the nucleus.

title: Pivotal roles of PCNA loading and unloading in heterochromatin function.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
reason: PCNA loading and unloading by Elg1 in maintaining HML and HMR silencing in budding yeast; replication machinery dynamics on chromatin but a different organism and a heterochromatin maintenance question.

title: Distribution of PCNA during Postblastoderm Cell Division Cycles in the Drosophila melanogaster Embryo: Effect of a string- Mutation.
reason: Immunocytochemical PCNA distribution across Drosophila postblastoderm divisions, with signal loss at mitosis attributed to reorganisation of PCNA within a nuclear complex; insect embryo entering mitosis rather than mammalian cells leaving the cycle.

title: Microfilament reorganization during apoptosis: the role of Gas2, a possible substrate for ICE‐like proteases.
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): cytoplasmic microfilament reorganisation and Gas2 cleavage during apoptosis; shares only the word reorganisation with the question.

title: Dentate Granule Cell Neurogenesis Is Increased by Seizures and Contributes to Aberrant Network Reorganization in the Adult Rat Hippocampus
reason: Seizure-induced dentate granule cell neurogenesis and mossy fibre network reorganisation in rat hippocampus; a neuroanatomical remodelling study unrelated to nuclear replication machinery.

title: Superresolution imaging reveals spatiotemporal propagation of human replication foci mediated by CTCF-organized chromatin structures
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Superresolution mapping of individual human replication foci reveals a hierarchical radial propagation pattern that reverses direction across S phase, substantive evidence on spatial organisation of replication in the mammalian nucleus but in proliferating cells only.

title: Processi di differenziamento neuronale: lezioni da modelli di neuroblastoma
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): neuronal differentiation lessons from neuroblastoma models; nothing in the title touches replication machinery or its nuclear distribution.

title: Building a nuclear envelope at the end of mitosis: coordinating membrane reorganization, nuclear pore complex assembly, and chromatin de-condensation
reason: Post-mitotic nuclear envelope formation, nuclear pore assembly and chromatin de-condensation; concerns rebuilding the envelope after division, not replication foci repositioning.

title: Characterization and function of the nek11 kinase in cancer cells
reason: Nek11 kinase in the G2/M checkpoint and chemosensitivity of colorectal cancer cells; a checkpoint signalling and therapy study with no nuclear replication machinery imaging.

title: Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA): a dancer with many partners
reason: Review of PCNA and its many interaction partners, noting that PCNA temporally and spatially organises partner functions; general background on the machinery rather than its nuclear redistribution at cycle exit.

title: PCNA appears in two populations of slow and fast diffusion with a constant ratio throughout S-phase in replicating mammalian cells
reason: Single-particle tracking in live mammalian cells resolves a slow PCNA population inside replication foci and a fast nucleoplasmic pool with defined exploration radii, quantitative detail on how replication machinery is spatially distributed, but measured only across S phase in replicating cells.

title: Regulation of Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen during the Cell Cycle
reason: Measures PCNA synthesis rate, stability and abundance across the HeLa cell cycle and notes reduced levels in nongrowing cells; an abundance study, not a nuclear localisation one.

title: Molecular and cellular analysis of topography-induced mechanotransduction
reason: Topography-induced mechanotransduction on microgrooved quartz substrata across chromosome, RNA and protein levels; a cell-material interaction study unrelated to replication foci placement.

title: Spatial perspectives in the redox code-Mass spectrometric proteomics studies of moonlighting proteins.
reason: Mass-spectrometry proteomics of redox-driven subcellular protein trafficking and moonlighting proteins; the spatial reorganisation described is proteome-wide relocation under oxidative stress, not replication machinery in the nucleus at cycle exit.

title: Nuclear lamins: building blocks of nuclear architecture
reason: Lamin structure and function review noting nucleoplasmic lamins and lamin involvement in DNA synthesis; background on the nuclear scaffold that anchors replication sites, without addressing the exit question.

title: Rescue of DNA damage after constricted migration reveals a mechano-regulated threshold for cell cycle
reason: Nuclear rupture and DNA damage caused by constricted migration through pores and the resulting reversible cell cycle block; a mechanobiology study, not spatial reorganisation of replication machinery.

title: Nuclear Dynamics of PCNA in DNA Replication and Repair
reason: GFP-PCNA photobleaching and foci tracking in living cells quantifies the equilibrium between bound and mobile PCNA and its accumulation at damaged sites across cell cycle stages, real evidence on nuclear dynamics of the replication clamp but framed around replication and repair, not cycle exit.

title: Distribution of PCNA in Drosophila embryo during nuclear division cycles
reason: Immunocytochemical PCNA localisation across the first 13 Drosophila syncytial division cycles, including dissociation from metaphase chromosomes and cytoplasm-to-nucleus transport; a non-mammalian embryo and mitotic rather than exit-related redistribution.

title: The second half of mitosis and its implications in cancer biology
reason: Review of mitotic exit and nuclear reformation with links to cancer biology; nuclear reassembly after division is a different event from replication machinery reorganisation before quiescence.

title: Quantitative kinetic analysis of nucleolar breakdown and reassembly during mitosis in live human cells
reason: Quantitative 4D imaging of nucleolar disassembly and reassembly through mitosis in human cells; tracks nucleolar subcompartments and RNA polymerase I, not replication machinery or cycle exit.

title: The p21 and PCNA partnership: A new twist for an old plot
reason: Reviews p21 as a negative regulator of translesion synthesis through its CDK and PCNA binding domains; couples a cell cycle inhibitor to PCNA but the subject is TLS fidelity, not nuclear repositioning of replication sites.

title: Histochemical and immunohistochemical analysis of testicular morphology and spermatogenesis in Gymnotus carapo (Teleostei: Gymnotidae).
reason: Testicular morphology and spermatogenesis in the fish Gymnotus carapo with PCNA used as a proliferation stain; a reproductive-biology description with no nuclear replication machinery analysis.

title: Multiple roles of the proliferating cell nuclear antigen: DNA replication, repair and cell cycle control
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): a review of PCNA roles in replication, repair and cell cycle control provides general background on the machinery but promises no spatial or cycle-exit findings.

title: Stable chromosomal units determine the spatial and temporal organization of DNA replication
reason: Live HeLa imaging shows DNA is not redistributed during S phase and that the replication machinery moves sequentially through stable sub-chromosomal foci, directly addressing spatial organisation of replication in mammalian nuclei though not the approach to cycle exit.

title: Role of histone methylation in paternal transmission of epigenetic information
reason: Histone-to-protamine exchange and paternal transmission of epigenetic information; germline chromatin reorganisation, unrelated to replication machinery position in somatic nuclei.

title: Spatial regulation and organization of DNA replication within the nucleus
reason: Review devoted to how DNA replication is spatially organised within the nucleus in replication factories and how that couples to timing, squarely on the spatial-organisation half of the question, but centred on budding and fission yeast and silent on mammalian cycle exit.

title: PCNA on the crossroad of cancer
reason: Reviews PCNA post-translational modification and partner exchange at stalled forks in the context of cancer; machinery-level background without nuclear spatial reorganisation or quiescence.

title: Analysis of the morphogenesis and cell proliferation in the retina of a pleuronectiform fish, the turbot Psetta maxima (Pleuronectiformes: Teleostei).
reason: PCNA immunohistochemistry of retinal morphogenesis and proliferative germinal zones in turbot larvae; tissue-level spatial cell reorganisation in a fish, not intranuclear replication machinery.

title: Targeting of PCNA to sites of DNA replication in the mammalian cell nucleus*
reason: Confocal and GFP-PCNA analysis in human diploid fibroblasts quantifies PCNA colocalisation with early, middle and late S-phase replication sites and shows PCNA disassembling from replicated sites and retargeting to newly active ones, a substantial part of the answer for proliferating rather than exiting cells.

title: Temporally coordinated assembly and disassembly of replication factories in the absence of DNA synthesis
reason: Graded on title alone (no abstract): temporally coordinated assembly and disassembly of replication factories in the absence of DNA synthesis speaks directly to how replication machinery organisation is maintained when synthesis is uncoupled, close to the asked question though the exit condition is unstated.

title: The DNA replication apparatus in Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes
reason: Immunofluorescence of Pcna, Rfc and topoisomerases in Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes including stages without DNA synthesis; an interesting parallel but a protozoan parasite, not mammalian cells leaving the cycle.

title: Protective effect of nebivolol on rat ovary exposed to deltamethrin toxicity.
reason: Nebivolol protection against deltamethrin ovarian toxicity in rats, with PCNA and TNF-alpha used as immunohistochemical markers; a toxicology study sharing only the PCNA term.

title: Monoclonal antibody analysis of the proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) structural conservation and the detection of a nucleolar form

title: Effects of heavy metals and nitroaromatic compounds on horseradish glutathione S-transferase and peroxidase
reason: Judged on title alone (no abstract available). title: Nitric Oxide Inhibition of Tobacco Catalase and Ascorbate Peroxidase
reason: Nitric oxide and peroxynitrite inhibiting tobacco catalase and ascorbate peroxidase. title: Mutagenic activity of promutagens in plants: indirect evidence of their activation
journal: Mutation research. Fundamental and molecular mechanisms of mutagenesis
reason: Judged on title alone (no abstract available). Mutagenic activity of promutagens in plants is background on plant-mediated genotoxicity of xenobiotics; it does not report protective enzyme responses or nitrobenzene-type exposure in tobacco leaves.

title: The effect of nitrobenzene on antioxidative enzyme activity and DNA damage in tobacco seedling leaf cells.
reason: Exactly the question: nitrobenzene dosed to tobacco seedlings, with H2O2 and superoxide content, SOD, POD and CAT activities, and comet-assay H-DNA, T-DNA and OTM DNA damage in leaf cells. This is the paper a researcher would cite as the answer.

title: Carbofuran cytotoxicity, DNA damage, oxidative stress, and cell death in human umbilical vein endothelial cells: Evidence of vascular toxicity
reason: Carbofuran cytotoxicity, ROS and comet OTM DNA damage in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Pesticide oxidative stress and genotoxicity in a mammalian cell model; no plant tissue and no antioxidant enzyme activity measurements.

reason: Measures half-lives of B77 ASV genomic and subgenomic RNAs versus cellular mRNA in infected chicken embryo fibroblasts, giving baseline turnover for the same species; useful context for accumulation arguments but no methylation or inhibitor treatment.

title: High-Resolution Analysis of Cytosine Methylation in the 5′ Long Terminal Repeat of Retroviral Vectors
reason: Bisulfite mapping of CpG methylation in Mo-MuLV vector 5' LTRs and its inverse correlation with transgene expression in F9 and fibroblast cells; DNA methylation of a vector promoter, unrelated to spliced viral mRNA accumulation under methyl-donor depletion.

title: Rev and the fate of pre-mRNA in the nucleus: implications for the regulation of RNA processing in eukaryotes.
reason: Shows HIV-1 intron-containing pre-mRNA is retained and degraded in the nucleus without Rev. Related theme of nuclear fate of retroviral transcripts, but it explains loss of unspliced RNA in a complex retrovirus and involves no methylation.

title: The emerging biology of RNA post-transcriptional modifications
reason: Broad review of post-transcriptional RNA modifications across tRNA, rRNA and mRNA and their dynamic responses to stress; general background on modification function with no retroviral splicing or methyl-donor depletion content.

title: cis-acting intron mutations that affect the efficiency of avian retroviral RNA splicing: implication for mechanisms of control
reason: Avian sarcoma virus intron mutations near the env splice acceptor that shift the spliced/unspliced balance, concluding cis-acting sequences control splicing efficiency. Same system and same readout, but the determinant is sequence, not methylation status.

title: Cycloleucine blocks 5'-terminal and internal methylations of avian sarcoma virus genome RNA
reason: Defines the methyl-depleted condition itself: cycloleucine lowers S-adenosylmethionine and blocks >90% of internal m6A and the penultimate 2'-O-ribose methylation of B77 ASV genome RNA while leaving cap m7G and virus production intact. It supplies the biochemical basis of the defect but examines genome RNA, not spliced mRNA accumulation.

title: The RNA Modification N 6-Methyladenosine and Its Implications in Human Disease
reason: Review of m6A writers, erasers and readers and their links to human disease and viral infection; provides the epitranscriptomic framework but does not address avian retroviral splicing or SAM depletion.

title: Characterization and partial purification of mRNA N6-adenosine methyltransferase from HeLa cell nuclei. Internal mRNA methylation requires a multisubunit complex
reason: Characterizes and partially purifies the multisubunit HeLa mRNA N6-adenosine methyltransferase and its S-adenosylmethionine-binding component. Enzymology background for why SAM loss abolishes m6A, but it makes no claim about splicing or viral mRNA accumulation.

title: Extensive Epitranscriptomic Methylation of A and C Residues on Murine Leukemia Virus Transcripts Enhances Viral Gene Expression
reason: Demonstrates that m6A, m5C and Nm modifications on murine leukemia virus transcripts are needed for efficient viral gene expression, with mutational removal inhibiting replication in cis. Answers the analogous question of why loss of RNA methylation depresses retroviral RNA function, for a different retrovirus and without methyl-donor depletion.

title: m6A RNA methylation regulates the fate of endogenous retroviruses
reason: Title only (no abstract): m6A RNA methylation regulating the fate of endogenous retroviruses. Directly couples RNA methylation to retroviral transcript fate, the same mechanistic axis as the question, though for endogenous retroviruses rather than methyl-depleted avian cells.

title: Mammalian WTAP is a regulatory subunit of the RNA N6-methyladenosine methyltransferase
reason: Identifies WTAP and METTL14 as m6A methyltransferase complex components localizing to pre-mRNA processing speckles and notes effects on alternative splicing; machinery-level background rather than an account of methyl-depleted retroviral mRNA.

title: Split-Intron Retroviral Vectors: Enhanced Expression with Improved Safety
reason: Engineering report on split-intron retroviral vectors that copy a synthetic splice donor during reverse transcription to boost transgene expression; a gene-therapy vector design problem sharing only splicing and retrovirus vocabulary.

title: Selective inhibition of avian sarcoma virus protein synthesis in 3-deazaadenosine-treated infected chicken embryo fibroblasts
reason: Uses the methylation inhibitor 3-deazaadenosine in B77-infected chicken embryo fibroblasts and reports selective inhibition of viral RNA accumulation, with genome-sized 35S/38S RNA reduced relative to the 28S and 21S mRNAs and matching shifts in viral protein synthesis. Same system and same class of perturbation, so it addresses how blocking methylation reshapes viral RNA pools, though the reported imbalance runs opposite to the asked observation.

title: RNA modifications go viral
reason: Short primer describing the cellular m6A writers, erasers and readers, including YTHDC1 regulation of m6A pre-mRNA splicing, in cellular and viral RNA; orienting background, with no experiment bearing on avian retroviral mRNA accumulation.

title: Particles of reduced infectivity and deficient in envelope glycoproteins are produced in cycloleucine-treated B77 avian sarcoma virus-infected chicken embryo fibroblasts.
reason: Follow-up in the identical cycloleucine-treated B77-infected chicken embryo fibroblast system showing particles that retain reverse transcriptase but are depleted of gp85/gp37 and poorly infectious, the predicted consequence of the missing spliced env mRNA. Confirms and extends the phenomenon rather than explaining the splicing block itself.

title: Endogenous avian retroviruses contain deficient promoter and leader sequences.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Compares LTR promoter strength of exogenous and endogenous avian retroviruses and finds an extra defect in the ev-1 5' leader; avian retroviral gene expression, but the question addressed is transcription initiation, not methylation-dependent mRNA accumulation.

title: Control of retroviral RNA splicing through maintenance of suboptimal processing signals.
reason: Avian sarcoma virus env splicing shown to be held in check by suboptimal cis-acting processing signals, independent of viral proteins and the donor site. Same system and same spliced/unspliced balance question, but the explanation offered is sequence suboptimality rather than a methyl-donor requirement.

title: Active specific immunotherapy: PEM as a potential target molecule.
reason: PEM here means polymorphic epithelial mucin as a tumour target for active specific immunotherapy; no hepatic macrophages, no guinea pig, only the acronym overlaps.

title: Genetically Restricted Immune Responses in Guinea Pigs Primed in Vivo with Antigen-Bearing Macrophages
reason: Guinea pigs primed in vivo with antigen-pulsed macrophages generate MHC-restricted proliferating T cells; answers macrophage antigen presentation to lymphocytes for peritoneal rather than hepatic macrophages.

title: Immunopeptidomics reveals determinants of Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen presentation on MHC class I
reason: Immunopeptidomics of MHC-I presentation of M. tuberculosis peptides by human macrophages; antigen presentation topic but different species, cell source and question than isolated guinea pig liver macrophages.

title: 3AE8: Monoclonal Antibody Defining Inflammatory Macrophages in Three Species
reason: Monoclonal antibody 3AE8 distinguishes inflammatory exudate from resident macrophages in rabbit, mouse and rat and enhances phagocytosis; useful macrophage-subset context but no antigen presentation to lymphocytes.

title: Reversible Paraneoplastic Encephalomyelitis Associated with a Benign Ovarian Teratoma
journal: Canadian Journal of Neurological Sciences / Journal Canadien des Sciences Neurologiques
reason: Case report of paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis with ovarian teratoma; PEM abbreviation collision only, nothing about macrophages or antigen presentation.

title: Identification of a Subpopulation of Macrophages in Mammary Tumor–Bearing Mice That Are Neither M1 nor M2 and Are Less Differentiated
reason: Mouse mammary-tumour peritoneal macrophage differentiation and inflammatory cytokine deficiency; different subject with no lymphocyte antigen presentation and no liver macrophages.

title: MACROPHAGE-LYMPHOCYTE CLUSTERS IN THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO SOLUBLE PROTEIN ANTIGEN IN VITRO
reason: Ultrastructure of macrophage-lymphocyte clusters formed by guinea pig peritoneal exudate cells and lymph node T cells responding to PPD; same macrophage-lymphocyte antigen interaction but peritoneal, not hepatic, cells.

title: Photosensitive erythema multiforme and its dramatic response to dapsone and the mechanism therein
reason: Dermatology case of photosensitive erythema multiforme treated with dapsone; PEM acronym clash, no macrophage or antigen-presentation content.

title: Lack of binding of bacterial lipopolysaccharide to mouse lung macrophages and restoration of binding by gamma interferon.
reason: Compares LPS binding and tumoricidal activation of mouse resident peritoneal, exudate and lung macrophages; tissue macrophage heterogeneity as background, but no antigen presentation to lymphocytes.

title: Nature of the antigenic complex recognized by T lymphocytes. I. Analysis with an in vitro primary response to soluble protein antigens.
reason: In vitro primary sensitisation of naive guinea pig T cells by antigen-pulsed macrophages with MHC-restricted rechallenge; the same question answered for peritoneal macrophages rather than Kupffer cells.

title: FUNCTION OF MACROPHAGES IN ANTIGEN RECOGNITION BY GUINEA PIG T LYMPHOCYTES
reason: Shows guinea pig macrophage-lymphocyte cooperation is required for antigen-driven T cell DNA synthesis and needs MHC identity; core antigen-presentation finding for non-hepatic macrophages.

title: A phase II study of pembrolizumab in combination with mFOLFOX6 for patients with advanced colorectal cancer.
reason: Phase II trial of pembrolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 in colorectal cancer; PEM stands for the drug, unrelated to hepatic macrophages presenting antigen.

title: Immunological reactivity of the lung I. A guinea pig model for the study of pulmonary mononuclear cell subpopulations
reason: No abstract available; judged on title alone. A guinea pig model of pulmonary mononuclear cell subpopulations is same-organism macrophage background, but lung-focused and not about antigen presentation by liver macrophages.

title: Primary ectopic meningioma in the thoracic cavity: A rare case report and review of the literature.
reason: Case report of primary ectopic meningioma in the thoracic cavity; only the PEM abbreviation is shared with the question.

title: The G Protein-Coupled Receptor GPR31 Promotes Pro-inflammatory Responses in Pancreatic Islets and Macrophages
reason: GPR31 and 12-HETE driving pro-inflammatory responses in pancreatic islets and bone marrow macrophages in diabetes models; different subject with no antigen presentation to lymphocytes.

title: Characterization of Isolated Guinea Pig Kupffer Cells: Accessory Cell Function in Mitogen-Induced T Lymphocyte Activation
reason: Isolated and purified guinea pig Kupffer cells restore mitogen-induced T lymphocyte proliferation as accessory cells, compared with peritoneal exudate macrophages; exact cell population but mitogen rather than antigen presentation.

title: Immunologic Function of Kupffer Cells
reason: No abstract available; graded on the title alone. 'Immunologic Function of Kupffer Cells' covers the immune role of hepatic resident macrophages, so it supplies substantial context on their accessory/antigen-presenting capacity.

title: Chemotherapy Immunophenoprofiles in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer by Personalized Membrane Proteomics.
reason: Membrane proteomics of PBMCs after pemetrexed-cisplatin chemotherapy in lung cancer patients; PEM is the drug and no macrophage antigen presentation is studied.

title: Structural and computational investigations of the conformation of antigenic peptide fragments of human polymorphic epithelial mucin
reason: NMR and Monte Carlo conformational study of polymorphic epithelial mucin peptide epitopes; structural chemistry of an antigen, not macrophage presentation to lymphocytes.

title: Therapeutic cancer vaccines: advancements, challenges and prospects
reason: Broad review of therapeutic cancer vaccines and antigen delivery; shares only the generic term antigen presentation, no hepatic macrophage or guinea pig work.

title: Antigen presentation by isolated guinea pig Kupffer cells.
reason: Directly titled and executed as antigen presentation by isolated guinea pig Kupffer cells: Ag-pulsed KC induce MHC-restricted proliferation of primed T lymphocytes, less efficiently than peritoneal macrophages. This is the answer.

title: Detection of live M. bovis BCG in tissues and IFN-γ responses in European badgers (Meles meles) vaccinated by oropharyngeal instillation or directly in the ileum
reason: Oral BCG vaccination and IFN-gamma responses in badgers; different species, tissue and question, unrelated to hepatic macrophage antigen presentation.

title: Abrogation of species specificity for activation of tumoricidal properties in macrophages by recombinant mouse or human interferon-gamma encapsulated in liposomes.
reason: Liposomal recombinant IFN-gamma plus MDP activating tumoricidal monocytes and peritoneal exudate macrophages; macrophage effector activation, not antigen presentation to lymphocytes.

title: Identification and characterization of autoreactive T cell responses to bullous pemphigoid antigen 2 in patients and healthy controls.
reason: Autoreactive T cell responses to bullous pemphigoid antigen 2 in patients and controls; human autoimmunity with PBMC, no macrophage or hepatic component.

title: Liver sinusoidal lining cells express class II major histocompatibility antigens but are poor stimulators of fresh allogeneic T lymphocytes.
reason: Isolated guinea pig liver sinusoidal lining cells (Kupffer plus endothelial cells) are assessed as antigen-presenting cells: class II positive but poor stimulators of fresh allogeneic T cells; supplies a real part of the answer, though tested by allostimulation rather than nominal antigen.

title: The Expression of Ia Antigens on Immunocompetent Cells in the Guinea Pig
reason: Ia-negative guinea pig macrophages are deficient at presenting protein antigens to immune T lymphocytes, identifying the presenting subpopulation; same question for oil-induced peritoneal, not hepatic, macrophages.

title: Human antibodies against the polymorphic epithelial mucin in ovarian cancer patients recognise a novel sequence in the tandem repeat region.
reason: Human antibody epitope mapping on the polymorphic epithelial mucin tandem repeat in ovarian cancer; humoral response to a mucin, unrelated to liver macrophages.

title: Specificity of bispecific T cell receptors and antibodies targeting peptide-HLA.
reason: Specificity of bispecific TCR and TCR-mimic antibodies against peptide-HLA for cancer therapeutics; molecular targeting study with no macrophage antigen presentation.

title: The expression of Ia antigens on immunocompetent cells in the guinea pig. II. Ia antigens on macrophages.
reason: Companion report that Ia antigens mark the guinea pig macrophage subpopulation able to present protein antigens to immune T cells; addresses macrophage presentation but in peritoneal exudate cells.

title: Exploring the Effects of Pemivibart Monoclonal Antibody Infusion in Long COVID: A Case Series Offering Initial Clinical Insights
reason: Case series of pemivibart monoclonal antibody infusion in Long COVID, where PEM means postexertional malaise; no overlap with macrophage antigen presentation.

title: Defective antigen presentation in chronically protein-deprived mice.
reason: Defective antigen presentation by splenic APCs in protein-energy malnourished mice, with reduced Ia and IL-1; antigen-presentation subject area but different species, cell source and causal question.

title: THE FATE OF PERITONEAL MACROPHAGES AFTER THE INJECTION OF ANTIGEN INTO GUINEA PIGS WITH DELAYED-TYPE HYPERSENSITIVITY.
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. Fate of peritoneal macrophages after antigen injection into guinea pigs with delayed hypersensitivity concerns macrophage trafficking, not presentation by liver macrophages.

title: Using Milk-derived Exosomes To Repair Malnutrition-induced Gut Barrier Dysfunction In Mice
reason: Milk-derived exosomes repairing malnutrition-induced gut barrier dysfunction in mice; intestinal stem cell and permeability subject, entirely different from the question.

title: Peroxidase cytochemistry and ultrastructure of resident macrophages in fetal rat liver
reason: No abstract available; title only. Peroxidase cytochemistry and ultrastructure of resident macrophages in fetal rat liver concerns the same hepatic cell type but is morphological, with no lymphocyte or antigen work.

title: Macrophage Activation of Allogeneic Lymphocyte Proliferation in the Guinea Pig Mixed Leukocyte Culture
reason: Guinea pig macrophages from peritoneum, spleen and alveoli act as the main stimulators in mixed leukocyte culture; alloreactive stimulation rather than antigen presentation, and no hepatic cells examined.

title: THE RELATIVE IMPORTANCE OF BLOOD MONOCYTES AND FIXED MACROPHAGES TO THE EXPRESSION OF CELL-MEDIATED IMMUNITY TO INFECTION
reason: Monocyte-derived versus Kupffer cell contribution to antilisterial immunity in mouse liver; liver macrophage biology as background, but the readout is antimicrobial effector immunity, not antigen presentation.

title: The Function of Macrophages in Antigen Recognition by Guinea Pig T Lymphocytes
reason: Activation of immune T lymphocytes by antigen-pulsed guinea pig macrophages is mediated by Ia/Ir gene products; substantive macrophage antigen-presentation result for non-hepatic macrophages.

title: Immunotherapeutic Agents for Intratumoral Immunotherapy
reason: Review of intratumoral immunotherapeutic agents, checkpoint inhibitors and CAR T cells; shares only general immunology vocabulary with the question.

title: Alterations in Macrophage-Produced Cytokines and Nitrite Associated with Poult Enteritis and Mortality Syndrome
reason: Cytokine and nitrite output by abdominal macrophages in turkey poult enteritis and mortality syndrome; PEMS acronym clash, macrophage inflammatory mediators rather than antigen presentation.

title: Antigen presentation by liver sinusoidal lining cells after antigen exposure in vivo.
reason: Guinea pig liver sinusoidal lining cells, including Kupffer cells, take up intraportal TNP-ovalbumin in vivo and present it to primed syngeneic T lymphocytes in an antigen-specific, genetically restricted way; directly answers the question.

title: Antigen-Induced Proliferation of Guinea Pig Lymphocytes in Vitro: Obligatory Role of Macrophages in the Recognition of Antigen by Immune T-Lymphocytes
reason: Demonstrates the obligatory role of macrophages in presenting PPD to primed guinea pig T lymphocytes, since antigen-pulsed lymphocytes alone cannot respond; same question for lymph node/peritoneal macrophages.

title: Cellular and Humoral Immunity in Guinea Pigs to Two Major Polypeptides Derived from Hepatitis B Surface Antigen
reason: Guinea pig cellular and humoral immunity to hepatitis B surface antigen polypeptides measured by macrophage migration inhibition; same organism and peritoneal exudate cells but the question is antigen immunogenicity.

title: Sex differences in cancer mechanisms
reason: Review of sex differences in cancer mechanisms and study design; no connection to macrophages, liver, or antigen presentation.

title: The polymorphic epithelial mucin: potential as an immunogen for a cancer vaccine.
reason: MUC1 polymorphic epithelial mucin as an immunogen for cancer vaccines in murine models; PEM is the mucin, not peritoneal or hepatic macrophages.

title: JQ 1, a Selective Bromodomain Inhibitor, Decreased the Expression of the Tolerogenic Molecule PDL1 in Antigen-Presenting Cells (APCs) and Restores the Responsiveness of Anergic CD4+ T Cells
reason: JQ1 bromodomain inhibition of mouse peritoneal elicited macrophages lowers PD-L1 and improves priming of anergic CD4 T cells; APC function is involved but the question is a pharmacologic one in mice, not hepatic macrophages.

title: The macrophage heterogeneity: Difference between mouse peritoneal exudate and splenic F4/80<sup>+</sup> macrophages
reason: Compares mouse peritoneal exudate and splenic F4/80+ macrophages for MHC-II, phagocytosis and T cell stimulation; tissue macrophage heterogeneity context, but neither liver macrophages nor guinea pigs.

title: Antigen Handling by Guinea Pig Macrophages: Further Evidence for the Sequestration of Antigen Relevant for Activation of Primed T Lymphocytes
reason: Shows guinea pig macrophages sequester the antigen fraction relevant to primed T lymphocyte activation in a trypsin- and antibody-inaccessible compartment; mechanism of macrophage antigen presentation, but not in Kupffer cells.

title: Crystallization of an antitumour antibody SM3 complexed with a peptide epitope
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section D Biological Crystallography
reason: Crystallisation report for the SM3 Fab bound to a mucin peptide epitope; structural biology of an antitumour antibody, no macrophage or lymphocyte assay.

title: Antigen presentation by guinea pig alveolar macrophages.
reason: Guinea pig alveolar macrophages act as effective antigen-presenting cells, Ia-dependent and genetically restricted, matching peritoneal exudate macrophages; the same question answered for a resident macrophage of another organ.

title: Biodegradable Polyelectrolyte Microcapsules: Antigen Delivery Tools with Th17 Skewing Activity after Pulmonary Delivery
reason: Polyelectrolyte microcapsules as pulmonary antigen delivery adjuvants skewing Th17 responses; PEM denotes a biomaterial, unrelated to hepatic macrophages.

title: More Than Just Attractive: How CCL2 Influences Myeloid Cell Behavior Beyond Chemotaxis
reason: Review of CCL2 effects on myeloid cell adhesion, polarisation and survival beyond chemotaxis; chemokine biology with no antigen presentation to lymphocytes by liver macrophages.

title: Macrophage tumor necrosis factor- alpha release is induced by contact with some tumors.
reason: Tumour cell contact triggering TNF-alpha release from elicited mouse peritoneal macrophages; macrophage effector secretion, a different subject from antigen presentation.

title: Polyelectrolyte Multilayers Assembled Entirely from Immune Signals on Gold Nanoparticle Templates Promote Antigen-Specific T Cell Response.
reason: Immune polyelectrolyte multilayer coatings on gold nanoparticles priming dendritic cells and CD8 T cells; PEM is a nanomaterial coating, not a macrophage population.

title: Tubastatin A, a Selective HDAC6 Inhibitor, Enhances Antigen-Presenting Cell (APC) Function and Restores the Responsiveness of Anergic CD4+ T Cells
reason: HDAC6 inhibition with Tubastatin A improves antigen presentation by mouse peritoneal elicited macrophages to HA-specific CD4 T cells; APC function is central but the question is drug modulation in mice, not liver macrophages.

title: NADPH oxidase activation regulates apoptotic neutrophil clearance by murine macrophages
reason: NADPH oxidase control of efferosome maturation during apoptotic neutrophil clearance by murine macrophages, with increased cross-presentation in CGD cells; antigen presentation is incidental to an efferocytosis study.

title: Length of the active-site crossover loop defines the substrate specificity of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases for ubiquitin chains.
reason: Title and abstract are explicitly about what defines UCH substrate specificity: long crossover loops let UCH-L5/BAP1 cleave both small and large Ub derivatives including K48-diUb, short loops only small derivatives.

title: Multiple Ubiquitin C-terminal Hydrolases from Chick Skeletal Muscle
reason: Reports the substrate range of ten chick muscle UCH activities: all release Ub from Ub-CEP80 and Ub-DHFR, five cleave diubiquitin, UCH-1 and UCH-7 cleave isopeptide-linked Ub, concluding they differ in substrate specificity.

title: Crystal structure of a deubiquitinating enzyme (human UCH‐L3) at 1.8 å resolution
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. A 1.8 A crystal structure of UCH-L3 is background on the enzyme but the title claims nothing about which substrates are preferred.

title: Friend or Foe: UCHL3 Mediated Carcinogenesis and Current Approaches in Small Molecule Inhibitors' Development.
reason: Review centred on UCHL3 in carcinogenesis and small molecule inhibitor discovery; substrate specificity is only named as something worth knowing for inhibitor design, not characterised.

title: Substrate specificity of deubiquitinating enzymes: ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases.
reason: Title is literally the substrate specificity of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases, and the abstract answers the question: UCH-L1/L3 prefer small leaving groups such as amino acids and oligopeptides and do not cleave large protein adducts or polyUb chains.

title: The Ubiquitin Binding Domain ZnF UBP Recognizes the C-Terminal Diglycine Motif of Unanchored Ubiquitin
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. The ZnF UBP domain (the proximal-Ub site of isopeptidase T) recognising the free C-terminal diglycine of unanchored ubiquitin explains why such isopeptidases prefer unanchored chain substrates.

title: Chemical Synthesis of Ubiquitinated Peptides with Varying Lengths and Types of Ubiquitin Chains to Explore the Activity of Deubiquitinases
reason: Synthesises peptides carrying mono- to tetraubiquitin in K48 or K63 linkage and uses them to compare UCH-L3 and IsoT activity, so it supplies comparative substrate-preference data even though synthesis is the headline.

title: Synthesis and characterization of ubiquitin ethyl ester, a new substrate for ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase
reason: Introduces ubiquitin C-terminal ethyl ester as a substrate for ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase and shows specific cleavage of the ester linkage plus competitive inhibition by native Ub, a real piece of the small-adduct preference picture.

title: Divergent N-terminal Sequences of a Deubiquitinating Enzyme Modulate Substrate Specificity
reason: Shows UBP-testis isoforms cleave branched triubiquitin over 20-fold faster than linear diubiquitin and that N-terminal extensions suppress cleavage of small adducts; substrate preference of a Ub C-terminal cleaving isopeptidase, though a UBP rather than a UCH.

title: Structural Basis for the Ubiquitin-Linkage Specificity and deISGylating Activity of SARS-CoV Papain-Like Protease
reason: Reports that SARS-CoV PLpro greatly prefers K48- over K63-linked chains and ISG15 over mono-ubiquitin, answering the substrate-preference question for a related viral deubiquitinating isopeptidase.

title: Biochemical Characterization and Substrate Specificity of Autophagin-2 from the Parasite Trypanosoma cruzi.
reason: Substrate specificity profiling of T. cruzi Atg4.2, an autophagy cysteine protease acting on Atg8, not a ubiquitin isopeptidase; UCH-L3 appears only as an enzyme that fails to cleave the peptides.

title: Specificity of the Ubiquitin Isopeptidase in the PA700 Regulatory Complex of 26 S Proteasomes
reason: Title and findings are the specificity of the PA700 ubiquitin isopeptidase: it removes only the distal Ub, requires Leu8/Ile44 there, disassembles K48-, K6- and K11-linked chains but not alpha-linked di-Ub.

title: Structure and activity of the essential UCH family deubiquitinase DUB16 from Leishmania donovani.
reason: Characterises the UCH-family isopeptidase DUB16 substrate by substrate: efficient on Ub C-terminal aminocoumarin and rhodamine adducts, poor on K11/K48/K63 diubiquitins, and 100-1000-fold faster on the ubiquitin-ribosomal L40 fusion.

title: Molecular cloning of chick UCH-6 which shares high similarity with human UCH-L3: its unusual substrate specificity and tissue distribution.
reason: Title advertises the unusual substrate specificity of chick UCH-6, and the abstract states that unlike other UCHs including UCH-L3 it releases Ub from ubiquitin-beta-galactosidase fusions in vivo and in vitro.

title: Ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase acts on ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal amides.
reason: Directly enumerates preferred substrates: Ub amides of lysine epsilon-amino, glycine methyl ester, spermidine and hydroxylamine are hydrolysed while Ub-protein lysine conjugates are much poorer, concluding high selectivity for small Ub derivatives.

title: Cathepsins X and B Can Be Differentiated through Their Respective Mono- and Dipeptidyl Carboxypeptidase Activities
reason: Substrate specificity of papain-family cathepsins X and B as mono- versus dipeptidyl carboxypeptidases; no ubiquitin, no isopeptidase activity, only the generic vocabulary of C-terminal cleavage and specificity.

title: Improved Quantitative Mass Spectrometry Methods for Characterizing Complex Ubiquitin Signals
reason: Mass spectrometry methodology for quantifying Ub linkage composition (K48, K63, K11) in samples; ubiquitin-system background with no measurement of isopeptidase substrate preference.

title: Recognition of Polyubiquitin Isoforms by the Multiple Ubiquitin Binding Modules of Isopeptidase T
reason: Maps how isopeptidase T's ZnF UBP, UBP and two UBA domains engage linear and K48-linked polyubiquitin across at least four binding sites, supplying substrate-recognition determinants for a Ub C-terminal cleaving isopeptidase.

title: Citrate-capped gold nanoparticles for the label-free detection of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase-1
reason: Gold nanoparticle assay for detecting UCH-L1 as a brain-injury biomarker; the engineered thiol-tagged Ub is an assay reagent, and no comparison of natural substrate preferences is made.

title: Proteome-derived Peptide Libraries to Study the Substrate Specificity Profiles of Carboxypeptidases
reason: Proteome-derived peptide library profiling of metallocarboxypeptidases hCPA1/A2/A4, mCPA3 and prolylcarboxypeptidase; a different enzyme class with no ubiquitin or isopeptide bond involvement.

title: Mechanism and function of deubiquitinating enzymes
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Cell Research
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. A broad review of deubiquitinating enzyme mechanism and function is useful background but the title promises no specific substrate-preference findings.

title: Structure and mechanisms of the proteasome‐associated deubiquitinating enzyme USP14
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. Structure and mechanism of the proteasomal DUB USP14 sits in the same enzyme area but the title addresses architecture and catalysis, not preferred substrates.

title: Metabolism of the polyubiquitin degradation signal: structure, mechanism, and role of isopeptidase T
reason: Defines isopeptidase T's substrate preferences precisely: an intact unblocked proximal RGG is required, rates fall when Gly76 is esterified, mutated or ligated, and linear proubiquitin is only a poor substrate.

title: Structural basis for the specificity of ubiquitin C‐terminal hydrolases
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone, but the title 'Structural basis for the specificity of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases' names exactly the enzyme family and the specificity question asked.

title: Substrate recognition and catalysis by UCH-L1.
reason: Examines substrate recognition by UCH-L1 using a panel of ubiquitin fusions, identifying the Ub side chains needed for the Michaelis complex and documenting dramatic substrate-specificity differences from UCH-L3.

title: Targeting of substrates to the 26S proteasome
reason: Concerns how K48-G76 polyubiquitin chains and antizyme target substrates to the 26S proteasome; ubiquitin-pathway background, with no analysis of what isopeptidases prefer to cleave.

title: A ubiquitin C-terminal isopeptidase that acts on polyubiquitin chains. Role in protein degradation.
reason: Characterises isopeptidase T's substrate requirements: it acts on polyUb-protein conjugates but not on methylated-Ub or K48R chains, releases Ub not protein, and stops after producing low-mass conjugates.

title: Ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases cleave isopeptide- and peptide-linked ubiquitin from structured proteins but do not edit ubiquitin homopolymers
reason: Screens UCH-family DUBs and reports exactly what they prefer: N-terminal peptide-linked and K11 isopeptide-linked Ub on structured proteins such as SUMO2 and Ube2W, with no activity on any of the eight Ub homopolymer linkages.

title: Characterizing Substrate Selectivity of Ubiquitin C-Terminal Hydrolase-L3 Using Engineered α-Linked Ubiquitin Substrates
reason: Title is the substrate selectivity of UCH-L3 measured with engineered alpha-linked Ub substrates, and it identifies thermal stability of the leaving group, not just size, as the determinant of hydrolysis.

title: Kinetic studies of isopeptidase T: modulation of peptidase activity by ubiquitin
reason: Ranks isopeptidase T substrate preference quantitatively across Z-GG-AMC through Z-Arg-Leu-Arg-Gly-Gly-AMC (kc/Km from <0.1 to 95 M-1 s-1), showing the extended Ub C-terminal sequence is what the isopeptidase prefers.

title: Structure of the ubiquitin hydrolase UCH-L3 complexed with a suicide substrate.
reason: Primarily a UCH-L3 structure with a suicide inhibitor, but it also demonstrates efficient hydrolysis of a 13-residue peptide in isopeptide linkage to Ub and argues for considerable flexibility in UCH substrate size.

title: Kinetic and Mechanistic Studies on the Hydrolysis of Ubiquitin C-Terminal 7-Amido-4-Methylcoumarin by Deubiquitinating Enzymes
reason: Compares kc/Km for Ub-AMC versus Z-Leu-Arg-Gly-Gly-AMC for isopeptidase T (10^4-fold) and UCH-L3 (>10^7-fold), quantifying how strongly these enzymes prefer substrates carrying the full Ub moiety.

title: Recent Developments in Techniques for Terminal and Sequence Studies in Peptides and Proteins
reason: A methods chapter on end-group analysis and stepwise sequencing of peptides (fluorodinitrobenzene, phenylisothiocyanate, carboxypeptidase); unrelated to ubiquitin or deubiquitinating enzymes.

title: The ubiquitin–proteasome pathway: on protein death and cell life
reason: No abstract available; graded on title alone. A general ubiquitin-proteasome pathway review is context for the enzyme family but the title indicates no substrate-specificity content.

title: Positional-scanning fluorigenic substrate libraries reveal unexpected specificity determinants of DUBs (deubiquitinating enzymes).
reason: Positional-scanning fluorigenic libraries define the preferred P4-P1 residues of OTU-1, isopeptidase T, UCH-L3 and PLpro, including UCH-L3's unusual tolerance of Ala and Val at P2, directly answering the specificity question.

title: Cathepsins X and B Display Distinct Activity Profiles That Can Be Exploited for Inhibitor Design
reason: Activity profiles and inhibitor design for cathepsins X, B and L; a papain-family carboxypeptidase study with no ubiquitin substrate or isopeptidase activity involved.
