reason: Review of machine learning and deep learning models for forecasting climate-driven outbreaks, focused on AI methods, data quality and interpretability; uses climate and environmental data as inputs rather than weighing drivers of transmission.

title: Vector Specificity of Arbovirus Transmission
reason: Reviews vector genetics, immunity, microbiome and some abiotic factors that determine arbovirus vector specificity and competence; molecular and physiological determinants, not landscape-scale climatic or socioeconomic drivers.

title: Disease ecology, health and the environment: a framework to account for ecological and socio-economic drivers in the control of neglected tropical diseases
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Presents a modelling framework for the relative role of ecological versus socio-economic drivers of neglected tropical disease transmission, including poverty-disease feedbacks; the same balancing question but illustrated with environmentally transmitted waterborne diseases rather than arthropod-borne ones.

title: Knowledge of Mongolian veterinarians towards canine vector-borne diseases.
reason: Questionnaire study scoring Mongolian veterinarians' knowledge of canine vector-borne disease; same general vector-borne field but the measured outcome is practitioner knowledge, not transmission drivers.

title: Current Topics in Tropical Emerging Diseases and Travel Medicine
reason: Book overview of tropical emerging diseases and travel medicine listing globalization, migration and travel as factors; too general and catalogue-like to address the balance of climatic, environmental and socioeconomic drivers.

title: Bluetongue virus spread in Europe is a consequence of climatic, landscape and vertebrate host factors as revealed by phylogeographic inference
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Phylogeographic models quantify climatic, landscape and host drivers of bluetongue virus spread, finding altitude, wind direction and livestock density important and no positive temperature effect; a rigorous driver comparison for one midge-borne system.

title: What are the vectors in European livestock farms? Case studies in Hungary and Spain
reason: Multi-vector inventory of mosquitoes, ticks and stable flies on Spanish and Hungarian farms; climatic, environmental and management influences are described qualitatively for arthropod abundance, with no measurement of transmission or of relative driver weight.

title: Climate change: A driver of increasing vector-borne disease transmission in non-endemic areas
reason: Centres on climate change as one driver among a multiplicity of biological, ecological, socioeconomic, demographic, migration and trade factors, and discusses the difficulty of attributing and quantifying climate against economic development and control successes; directly the balancing question.

title: Developing Models of Disease Transmission: Insights from Ecological Studies of Insects and Their Baculoviruses
reason: Concerns baculovirus epizootics in defoliating pest insects as a model system for transmission modelling and pest control; no arthropod vector of human or animal disease and no environmental or socioeconomic driver analysis.

title: Weather, host and vector – their interplay in the spread of insect-borne animal virus diseases
reason: Analyses how temperature, moisture and wind together with host migration and vector carriage govern spread of insect-borne animal virus diseases across endemic and epidemic zones; strong climatic and environmental driver content, no socioeconomic dimension.

title: Socio-Ecological Mechanisms Supporting High Densities of Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) in Baltimore, MD
reason: Hierarchical models test the relative roles of residential abandonment and income, vegetation and precipitation on Aedes albopictus infestation, including interactions between social and abiotic drivers; the asked-for balance, empirically resolved for one city and species.

title: Arthropod-borne diseases in Italy: from a neglected matter to an emerging health problem.
reason: Short overview cataloguing endemic and emerging arthropod-borne diseases in Italy; asserts susceptibility to climatic, environmental and socioeconomic change as framing but performs no assessment of those drivers.

title: Understanding pathogen survival and transmission by arthropod vectors to prevent human disease
reason: Reviews pathogen survival in the vector gut, microbiota, vector immunity and salivary factors, plus control strategies; mechanistic transmission biology rather than climatic, environmental or socioeconomic drivers.

title: Transmission risk of Oropouche fever across the Americas.
reason: Spatial epidemiology of Oropouche fever using satellite vegetation phenology finds landscape change and vegetation loss linked to outbreaks and notes transmission outside typical climatic conditions; an environmental-driver finding for one emerging arboviral disease.

title: Climate Change Drives the Transmission and Spread of Vector-Borne Diseases: An Ecological Perspective
reason: Synthesises nonlinear local climate effects, lagged ENSO and NAO effects and extreme events on VBD transmission and explicitly treats how interactions between non-climatic factors such as land use and human mobility and climatic factors shape transmission; addresses the driver balance head-on.

title: A review exploring the overarching burden of Zika virus with emphasis on epidemiological case studies from Brazil
reason: Reviews environmental (precipitation, humidity, temperature), anthropogenic (sanitation, urbanization, pollution) and socioeconomic (poverty, inequality, housing) risks for mosquito-borne Zika transmission; the full driver triad, scoped to one virus and Brazil.

title: Microclimate and host body condition influence mite population growth in a wild bird-ectoparasite system
journal: International Journal for Parasitology Parasites and Wildlife
reason: Experimental study of temperature, humidity, nest substrate and host condition on Northern Fowl Mite population growth in barn swallow nests; environmental drivers of ectoparasite abundance with no pathogen transmission component.

title: Impact of recent and future climate change on vector‐borne diseases
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
reason: Reviews recent and projected climate-driven shifts in vector and pathogen distribution across temperate, Arctic and highland regions and lists mobility, control measures, health services and political stability as additional determinants; the climatic-driver part in depth, other drivers only as caveats.

title: Assessing the impact of climate conditions on the distribution of mosquito species in Qatar.
reason: Naive Bayes model of temperature and humidity effects on the occurrence probability of mosquito species in Qatar; a single-country vector distribution model providing background rather than an account of transmission drivers and their balance.

title: Arthropod Vectors in a Rapidly Changing World: A Critical Review of Climate, Urban Growth, Land Conversion, and Emerging Disease Risk
reason: Critical review of how climatic warming, altered rainfall, urban growth, land conversion, invasion and human movement redistribute arthropod vectors, and criticises collapsing environmental suitability, vector establishment, exposure and realised transmission into one narrative; precisely the requested balancing.

title: Spatial variation in gender-biased parasitism: host-related, parasite-related and environment-related effects
reason: Examines host, parasite and environmental correlates of male-biased ectoparasite infestation in a South African rodent; involves ticks, mites, fleas and weather variables but answers a sex-bias question unrelated to disease transmission drivers.

title: Eco-Epidemiology of Vector-Borne Transmission of Trypanosoma cruzi in Domestic Habitats
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: eco-epidemiology of vector-borne Trypanosoma cruzi transmission in domestic habitats implies ecological and domestic/housing determinants of an arthropod-borne disease, which is a real part of the answer.

title: Global threats from invasive alien species in the twenty-first century and national response capacities
reason: Global analysis of invasive alien species threat and national response capacity; 'vectors' here means introduction pathways such as imports and air travel, with no arthropod-borne disease transmission content.

title: Thermal biology of mosquito‐borne disease
reason: Trait-based synthesis quantifying unimodal temperature dependence of transmission for 11 pathogens and 15 mosquito species with thermal optima and limits; a thorough answer for the climatic driver alone, with no environmental or socioeconomic weighing.

title: Invasive hematophagous arthropods and associated diseases in a changing world
reason: Traces how trade, transport, urbanization, climate change and the urban heat island interact to favour invasive hematophagous arthropods and the diseases they vector; covers climatic, land-use and globalization drivers, framed around invasion and management rather than transmission balance.

title: The importance of vector control for the control and elimination of vector-borne diseases
reason: History of vector control programmes, insecticide reliance and resistance, arguing for locally tailored evidence-based control; global environmental change is mentioned only in passing and drivers of transmission are not assessed.

title: Neglected tropical diseases risk correlates with poverty and early ecosystem destruction
reason: Compares environmental and socioenvironmental niche models for dengue, malaria, Chagas, leishmaniasis and spotted fever across a decade of Brazilian data, finding socioeconomic variables as important as environmental ones with GDP and vegetation loss the leading predictors; a direct quantitative weighing of the driver classes.

title: Scoping review on vector-borne diseases in urban areas: transmission dynamics, vectorial capacity and co-infection.
reason: Scoping review of urban VBD transmission dynamics and vectorial capacity that maps the evidence and identifies gaps specifically on climatic, environmental and socioeconomic factors; contributes evidence-mapping on the question for urban settings.

title: Environmental and social-demographic predictors of the southern house mosquito Culex quinquefasciatus in New Orleans, Louisiana
reason: Tests 22 environmental, weather and sociodemographic predictors of Culex quinquefasciatus abundance in New Orleans and finds weekly mean temperature and high-intensity developed land significant; an explicit climatic versus environmental versus sociodemographic comparison on the vector side.

title: Temperature impacts the environmental suitability for malaria transmission by Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles stephensi
reason: Mechanistic temperature-dependent suitability model for malaria transmission by Anopheles gambiae and stephensi, mapping thermal limits against observed prevalence; a detailed climatic-driver answer without environmental or socioeconomic factors.

title: Harmonizing Multisource Data to Inform Vector-Borne Disease Risk Management Strategies.
reason: Reviews data harmonization practice, partnerships and digital infrastructure needed for VBD risk management; the environmental degradation, climate and socioeconomic inequality triad is named as motivation, but the deliverable is data-practice recommendations rather than driver findings.

title: The Role of Temperature in Shaping Mosquito-Borne Viruses Transmission
reason: Synthesises temperature effects on arboviruses, their mosquito vectors and their interaction as an explanation for spread into temperate regions; substantive on the climatic driver only.

title: Frequency matters: How successive feeding episodes by blood-feeding insect vectors influences disease transmission
reason: Concerns how repeated blood meals in mosquitoes and sandflies alter vector competence and pathogen infection; a feeding-physiology determinant of transmission, unrelated to climatic, environmental or socioeconomic driver balance.

title: Gene Expression and Autoantibody Analysis Revealing Distinct Ancestry‐Specific Profiles Associated With Response to Rituximab in Refractory Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
reason: Whole blood transcript scores in adult SLE annotated to interferon, plasmablast, neutrophil and myeloid signatures, with interferon-high vs interferon-low/neutrophil-high clusters; supplies real modular interferon-heterogeneity data although the primary aim is predicting rituximab response.

title: Transcriptional profiling unveils type I and II interferon networks in blood and tissues across diseases
reason: Uses a modular strategy and separates type I IFN from IFN-gamma-inducible blood signatures, but the subject is mouse models of infection (Toxoplasma) and allergy/IL-17 lung inflammation, not adults with an autoimmune connective tissue disease; same technique, different problem.

title: Dissecting Interferon-Induced Transcriptional Programs in Human Peripheral Blood Cells
reason: Defines the distinct transcriptional programs elicited in human peripheral blood cells by IFN-alpha/beta/omega versus IFN-gamma and IL-12, which is the reference framework for separating type I from type II interferon signatures, but it is in vitro stimulation of healthy PBMCs rather than patients.

title: Microarray analysis of gene expression in lupus.
reason: Review of blood mononuclear cell microarray studies in lupus reporting the dominant interferon-induced gene expression pattern in SLE and juvenile dermatomyositis; addresses the blood interferon signature in systemic autoimmunity but not modular dissection of distinct interferon types.

title: Modular transcriptional repertoire analyses of adults with systemic lupus erythematosus reveal distinct type I and type II interferon signatures.
reason: Exactly the question: modular transcriptional repertoire analysis of adult SLE blood defines three IFN-annotated modules (M1.2, M3.4, M5.12) with distinct activation thresholds and attributes them to IFN-alpha, IFN-beta and IFN-gamma, giving a modular interferon score for patient stratification.

title: Measurement of Interferon Alpha Expression Using Multiple Methodologies Identifies a Signature in a Subgroup of Connective Tissue Disease Patients with Haematological Abnormalities
reason: Characterises the IFN-alpha signature across connective tissue diseases using three methods and identifies a signature-positive subgroup with haematological abnormalities; right disease family and interferon-signature stratification, but truncated abstract and restricted to IFN-alpha rather than a modular repertoire.

title: Transcriptome analysis unveils Th1 cell cycle signature as a distinctive feature of mixed connective tissue disease.
reason: Blood immune cell transcriptomics with gene modular analysis in adults with mixed connective tissue disease, but the reported distinctive feature is a Th1 cell cycle signature; the interferon signature appears only as a correlate, so it answers a different question in the same disease family.

title: Uncoupling interferons and the interferon signature explains clinical and transcriptional subsets in SLE
reason: Directly dissects distinct interferon patterns in adult SLE, showing IFN-I, IFN-II and IFN-III levels vary across clinical and transcriptional endotypes and that a large fraction of the interferon signature is IFN-independent; this is the heterogeneous-interferon answer asked for.

title: Categorization of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus using disease activity, patient-reported outcomes, and transcriptomic signatures.
reason: Adult SLE categorisation built from SLEDAI and an SF-36-derived type 2 symptom score; modular interferon signatures are only used to report that they did not differ between groups, so the subject is symptom-based clustering rather than interferon signature patterns.

title: Decoding lysophosphatidic acid signaling in physiology and disease: mapping the multimodal and multinodal signaling networks
reason: Review of lysophosphatidic acid signalling networks, receptors and ATX-targeted therapeutics across cancer and fibrosis; no blood transcriptional signature, no interferon, and no connective tissue disease cohort.

title: AutoCore: A network-based definition of the core module of human autoimmunity and autoinflammation
reason: Protein-protein interaction network map ('AutoCore') of 186 inborn errors of immunity subdivided into 19 endotypes; module language and autoimmunity classification overlap, but it is not a blood transcriptional interferon signature study in patients.

title: Type I interferon gene signature test–low and –high patients with systemic lupus erythematosus have distinct gene expression signatures
reason: Whole-blood transcriptome profiling of 681 adult SLE patients showing IFN gene signature test-high versus test-low patients carry distinct expression signatures, with IFN-beta/gamma/lambda/omega-specific signatures developed from stimulated blood; directly the distinct interferon patterns asked about.

title: Multi–cell type gene coexpression network analysis reveals coordinated interferon response and cross–cell type correlations in systemic lupus erythematosus
reason: Multi-cell-type coexpression network analysis of SLE patient blood identifies an interferon-stimulated gene module across cell types and stratifies patients into IFNneg and IFNpos groups; module-based blood interferon stratification, though only a binary interferon split rather than distinct interferon types.

title: Interferon pathway in SLE: one key to unlocking the mystery of the disease
reason: Review of interferon system activation and increased IFN-regulated gene expression in SLE that explicitly covers production of many different IFNs and the need for interferon-based patient stratification; substantive background on the blood interferon signature but not a modular analysis.

title: Differential regulation of the interferon response in systemic lupus erythematosus distinguishes patients of Asian ancestry
reason: Gene set variation analysis of multiple interferon gene signatures covering type 1 and type 2 IFN in sorted monocytes, B, T and NK cells of adult SLE patients, revealing differential interferon signature enrichment by ancestry; real interferon-heterogeneity data with an ancestry-focused question.

title: Transcription Factor STAT3 as a Novel Molecular Target for Cancer Prevention
reason: STAT3 as a drug target for cancer prevention and chemopreventive inhibitors; shares only generic transcription-factor and inflammation vocabulary, with no interferon signature or autoimmune connective tissue disease content.

title: POS0142 DISTINCT EXPRESSION CLUSTERS OF INTERFERON-REGULATED GENES ASSOCIATE DIFFERENTLY WITH DISEASE ACTIVITY IN PATIENTS WITH SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS.
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: distinct expression clusters of interferon-regulated genes associating differently with disease activity in SLE is precisely the distinct blood interferon patterns in adults with a systemic autoimmune connective tissue disease that was asked about.

title: Autoantibodies as Precision Tools in Connective Tissue Diseases: From Epiphenomenon to Endophenotype
reason: Review casting autoantibody repertoires as endophenotypes stratifying connective tissue diseases; correct disease family and mentions integration with transcriptomic data, but the subject is serological profiling rather than modular blood interferon signatures.

title: A novel two-score system for interferon status segregates autoimmune diseases and correlates with clinical features
reason: Builds a two-score interferon system from 31 ISGs selected from three IFN-annotated modules, validated in 328 autoimmune patients, showing IFN-Score-A and -B behave differently across SLE, RA and controls and track cutaneous and haematological activity; modular blood signatures giving distinct interferon patterns in adults.

title: Cell-Specific Type I IFN Signatures in Autoimmunity and Viral Infection: What Makes the Difference?
reason: Compares transcriptional type I interferon responses in CD4 T cells and monocyte subsets of SLE patients versus yellow fever vaccinees, identifying a shared IFN signature plus a pathogenic IFN-associated signature in lupus; supplies a real part of the interferon-pattern answer in patient blood cells.

title: Interferon-inducible gene expression signature in peripheral blood cells of patients with severe lupus
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Global PBMC expression profiling in SLE showing about half of patients carry a dysregulated IFN pathway signature marking severe renal, haematopoietic and CNS disease; foundational blood interferon signature with patient subgrouping, but no modular framework or interferon-type dissection.

title: IN SILICO DRUG REPURPOSING FOR INFLAMMATORY DISEASES: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF MOLECULAR DOCKING AND VIRTUAL SCREENING STUDIES
journal: American Journal of Advanced Technology and Engineering Solutions
reason: Systematic review of molecular docking and virtual screening for drug repurposing in inflammatory diseases; SLE is only named as one indication and there is no blood transcriptional or interferon signature analysis.

title: Identification of key biomarkers and immune infiltration in systemic lupus erythematosus by integrated bioinformatics analysis
reason: GEO-based bioinformatics screen of SLE datasets prioritising IFI27 and other interferon-inducible DEGs plus CIBERSORT immune infiltration; same disease and interferon-inducible genes, but the aim is single biomarker discovery, not modular interferon signature patterns.

title: Blood RNA-sequencing across the continuum of ANA-positive autoimmunity reveals insights into initiating immunopathology.
reason: Blood RNA-sequencing across the ANA-positive to SLE continuum reports an elevated modular interferon signature in progressors whose constituent genes are inducible by both type I and type II interferon; modular blood interferon analysis in adults, framed around progression risk.

title: Progression from at-risk state to clinical and severe systemic lupus erythematosus involves molecular dysregulations potentially reversible by biologics: implications for early diagnosis and treatment
reason: Blood RNA-seq with gene module-based clustering across at-risk, early SLE and lupus nephritis showing stepwise IFN-alpha/gamma amplification and module-eigengene heterogeneity; modular blood interferon signature data in adults, with progression and drug reversibility as the primary question.

title: OP0360 Rna-sequencing of 800 human blood samples reveals shared and unique expression profiles across seven systemic autoimmune diseases
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: RNA-sequencing of 800 blood samples finding shared and unique expression profiles across seven systemic autoimmune diseases is the same subject area, but the title names neither interferon patterns nor modular signatures.

title: T‐cell metabolism governing activation, proliferation and differentiation; a modular view
reason: Review of T-cell metabolic reprogramming during activation and differentiation; 'modular view' is used in an unrelated sense and there is no blood transcriptional signature or interferon analysis in connective tissue disease patients.

title: SLE Peripheral Blood B Cell, T Cell and Myeloid Cell Transcriptomes Display Unique Profiles and Each Subset Contributes to the Interferon Signature
reason: Sorted B, CD4 T and CD33+ myeloid transcriptomes from SLE patients show largely non-overlapping profiles with each subset contributing shared interferon signature transcripts; substantive dissection of where the blood interferon signature comes from in adult SLE.

title: Leucocyte subset-specific type 1 interferon signatures in SLE and other immune-mediated diseases
reason: Defines modules of type 1 interferon-associated genes by WGCNA in purified CD4, CD8, monocyte and neutrophil populations from SLE and other immune-mediated diseases, showing IFN-1 modules are overwhelmingly myeloid while T cell IFN-1 upregulation is SLE-restricted; modular blood signatures revealing distinct interferon patterns in adults.

title: Platelet transcriptional profile and protein expression in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: up-regulation of the type I interferon system is strongly associated with vascular disease
reason: Platelet microarray in adult SLE confirms a type I interferon gene signature and IFN-regulated proteins (PRKRA, IFITM1, CD69) that are elevated specifically in patients with vascular disease; a real interferon-signature pattern in patient blood cells, focused on cardiovascular risk.

title: Modeling Spatiotemporal Immune Dynamics in Inflammatory Diseases Using Integrative Multi-Modal Analytics and High-Dimensional Longitudinal Datasets
journal: World Journal of Biology Pharmacy and Health Sciences
reason: Proposes a multi-modal analytic framework (manifold alignment, tensor decomposition, dynamic Bayesian networks) for spatiotemporal immune dynamics in RA, IBD and SLE; methodological modelling paper with no interferon signature or modular blood transcriptional result.

title: Biological impact of iberdomide in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus.
reason: Phase 2b iberdomide pharmacodynamics in active SLE using Modular Immune Profiling gene expression, showing the type I IFN gene signature fell only in baseline IFN-high patients and efficacy tracked that signature; modular blood profiling with interferon-based stratification, in a drug-mechanism study.

title: Modular transcriptional repertoire analyses identify a blood neutrophil signature as a candidate biomarker for lupus nephritis.
reason: Same modular transcriptional repertoire method in adult SLE blood, but the reported signature is neutrophil module M5.15 as a lupus nephritis biomarker and it is explicitly not correlated with the IFN modules; same technique and disease, different signature question.

title: Interferon and Granulopoiesis Signatures in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Blood
reason: Blood microarray in active SLE identifies overexpression of interferon-induced genes alongside a granulopoiesis/immature granulocyte signature, with the interferon signature shut down by glucocorticoids; two distinct blood signatures in adult SLE, though not a modular repertoire or interferon-type analysis.

title: Btk-specific inhibition blocks pathogenic plasma cell signatures and myeloid cell-associated damage in IFNα-driven lupus nephritis.
reason: Btk inhibitor G-744 efficacy in IFN-alpha-accelerated NZB/W_F1 murine lupus nephritis; cross-species human modular repertoire analysis is used only to map plasma cell and myeloid pathology, so it is a mouse therapeutic study rather than interferon patterns in adult patients.

title: Identification of Regulatory Modules That Stratify Lupus Disease Mechanism through Integrating Multi-Omics Data
reason: Integrates SLE transcriptomic profiles with ChIP-seq-derived TF binding to build co-regulatory modules that explicitly stratify the common SLE interferon signature; module-based dissection of interferon signature heterogeneity in lupus blood and lymphocytes.

title: Sweet tailoring of glyco-modulatory extracellular matrix-inspired biomaterials to target neuroinflammation
reason: Glyco-engineered extracellular matrix-inspired biomaterials for neuroinflammation; entirely different subject with no interferon, blood transcriptomics or connective tissue disease content.

title: Modeling of clinical phenotypes in systemic lupus erythematosus based on the platelet transcriptome and FCGR2a genotype.
reason: Platelet RNA-seq in SLE mapped onto a modular landscape, but the question is FCGR2a genotype, proteinuria and coagulation/platelet activity modules; interferon signalling appears only as one enriched pathway, not as distinct interferon patterns.

title: Transcriptomic studies of systemic lupus erythematosus
reason: Review of SLE transcriptomic studies stating the interferon signature is complex, involving IFN-beta and IFN-gamma response genes beyond IFN-alpha, alongside myeloid/neutrophil and plasma cell signatures; summarises the distinct interferon patterns rather than reporting them primarily.

title: Human Bone Marrow Plasma Cell Atlas: Maturation and Survival Pathways Unraveled by Single Cell Analyses
reason: Single-cell atlas of 17,347 healthy human bone marrow antibody-secreting cells and long-lived plasma cell maturation; an IFN-responsive cluster is incidental and there is no autoimmune patient blood signature analysis.

title: An interferon-inducible neutrophil-driven blood transcriptional signature in human tuberculosis.
reason: Modular whole-blood transcriptional signature work, but the disease is active and latent tuberculosis with a neutrophil-driven IFN-inducible profile; SLE appears only as a comparison showing a different modular signature, so it is the same method on a different problem.

title: Association of the interferon signature metric with serological disease manifestations but not global activity scores in multiple cohorts of patients with SLE
reason: Derives a three-gene interferon signature metric (HERC5, EPSTI, CMPK2) from blood microarray data and splits adult SLE trial patients into stable ISM-High and ISM-Low subpopulations with differing serology; blood interferon signature stratification, but a binary metric rather than distinct interferon modules.

title: IRF4 and IRGs Delineate Clinically Relevant Gene Expression Signatures in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Rheumatoid Arthritis
reason: Peripheral blood IRF4 and interferon-responding gene (IFI44, IFI44L, IFI6, MX1) expression in SLE and RA yields three clusters of interferon-related gene expression signatures linked to severity and treatment outcome; real interferon signature heterogeneity in adult autoimmune patients.

title: Functionally impaired plasmacytoid dendritic cells and non-haematopoietic sources of type I interferon characterize human autoimmunity
reason: Addresses the cellular source of type I interferon, showing plasmacytoid dendritic cells are senescent non-effectors and keratinocyte IFN-kappa drives skin signatures in preclinical autoimmunity; the blood interferon signature is only a covariate, so it answers a different question.

title: The STAT4 SLE risk allele rs7574865[T] is associated with increased IL-12-induced IFN-γ production in T cells from patients with SLE
reason: Functional genetics of the STAT4 rs7574865 risk allele driving IL-12-induced IFN-gamma production and pSTAT4 in SLE T cells by flow cytometry; interferon biology in lupus but no blood transcriptional or modular signature analysis.

title: Transcriptional Blood Signatures Distinguish Pulmonary Tuberculosis, Pulmonary Sarcoidosis, Pneumonias and Lung Cancers
reason: Whole blood transcriptional profiling with an interferon-inducible neutrophil-driven signature, but the comparison set is tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, pneumonia and lung cancer; same modular blood signature approach applied to non-autoimmune pulmonary disease.

title: Identification of cellular senescence-associated hub genes and molecular targeting mechanisms of thalidomide in lupus nephritis (LN).
reason: Transcriptomic screen of lupus nephritis datasets for cellular senescence hub genes (CCL2, JUN, JAK2, FOS) plus thalidomide docking; same disease and network/modular analysis, but the question is senescence targets and drug binding, not interferon signature patterns.

title: Gossamer — a resource-efficient de novo assembler
reason: Gossamer is a memory-efficient de Bruijn de novo assembler; same general area of short-read assembly but it does not merge overlapping paired-end reads into longer fragments.

title: Fragment Merger: An Online Tool to Merge Overlapping Long Sequence Fragments
reason: Fragment Merger merges two to twelve overlapping long Sanger/chromatogram fragments for amplicon or gene assembly, not paired-end sequencing reads for de novo assembly, so it is the same technique on a different problem.

title: Normalized N50 assembly metric using gap-restricted co-linear chaining
reason: Proposes a normalized N50 metric for validating scaffold assemblies; assembly-quality background only, with no read-merging or read-extension method.

title: Pseudo-Sanger sequencing: massively parallel production of long and near error-free reads using NGS technology
reason: Pseudo-Sanger sequencing turns paired-end reads into long near error-free reads via local assembly of pairs that overlap at their ends, and shows a 5-fold de novo assembly N50 gain; a closely related read-lengthening approach, though it fills gaps rather than only merging overlaps.

title: The sequence and de novo assembly of the giant panda genome
reason: Reports the giant panda draft genome assembled from next-generation short reads; a de novo assembly application paper, not a paired-end read merging tool.

title: High contiguity Arabidopsis thaliana genome assembly with a single nanopore flow cell
reason: Arabidopsis assembly from a single nanopore flow cell; long-read genome assembly context with no paired-end read merging step.

title: Fast Short Read De-Novo Assembly Using Overlap-Layout-Consensus Approach
journal: IEEE Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
reason: MiniSR adapts an overlap-layout-consensus long-read pipeline to short-read de novo assembly; it is an assembler comparison, not a tool that merges overlapping read pairs.

title: An improved assembly and annotation of the allohexaploid wheat genome identifies complete families of agronomic genes and provides genomic evidence for chromosomal translocations
reason: Presents an improved wheat whole-genome shotgun assembly and annotation; genome assembly subject area but the question about merging overlapping paired reads is not addressed.

title: ngsShoRT
reason: ngsShoRT pre-processes Illumina reads by removing adapters and quality-trimming 3' ends to improve de novo assembly; a pre-assembly read-processing tool, but it trims rather than merges overlapping pairs.

title: TopHat: discovering splice junctions with RNA-Seq
reason: TopHat aligns RNA-Seq reads to a reference to discover splice junctions; a different problem (spliced alignment) with no relation to merging paired-end reads for de novo assembly.

title: Comparative studies of de novo assembly tools for next-generation sequencing technologies
reason: Benchmarks seven short-read de novo assemblers on N50, coverage and accuracy; useful assembly background, but no read-merging tool is described.

title: Konnector v2.0: pseudo-long reads from paired-end sequencing data
reason: Konnector v2.0 turns paired-end tag reads into pseudo-long reads by bridging the unsequenced gap between mates with a Bloom filter de Bruijn graph and is compared with tools of similar function; closely related read-connection tool, though it targets non-overlapping pairs.

title: Unicycler: Resolving bacterial genome assemblies from short and long sequencing reads
reason: Unicycler is a hybrid short plus long read bacterial assembler that simplifies an assembly graph; assembly area only, it does not merge overlapping read pairs into longer fragments.

title: Yet another de novo genome assembler
reason: Ra is a de novo assembler for long uncorrected reads based on sequence classification and assembly graphs; same field but not a paired-end merging pre-processor.

title: Optimizing Information in Next-Generation-Sequencing (NGS) Reads for Improving De Novo Genome Assembly
reason: ARF-PE takes Illumina paired-end reads and recovers the original DNA fragment spanned by each pair to lengthen reads, then quantifies the resulting N50 gains with Velvet, SOAPdenovo, Newbler and CABOG; this is exactly the asked-for read-to-fragment tool for improving de novo assembly.

title: Is the whole greater than the sum of its parts? De novo assembly strategies for bacterial genomes based on paired-end sequencing
reason: Systematically evaluates overlapping and merging paired-end reads of different library sizes for bacterial de novo assembly and reports when merging helps or hurts; supplies a real part of the answer even though it presents no new merging tool.

title: Pilon: An Integrated Tool for Comprehensive Microbial Variant Detection and Genome Assembly Improvement
reason: Pilon polishes draft assemblies and calls variants from aligned paired-end libraries; post-assembly correction rather than merging overlapping reads into longer fragments.

title: Nanopore sequencing and the Shasta toolkit enable efficient de novo assembly of eleven human genomes
reason: Shasta plus MarginPolish and HELEN assemble and polish human genomes from nanopore long reads; long-read assembly background with no paired-end read merging.

title: Initial sequencing and comparative analysis of the mouse genome
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: the initial mouse genome sequencing and comparative analysis paper is a genome survey, not a paired-end read merging tool.

title: De novo assembly of human genomes with massively parallel short read sequencing
reason: SOAPdenovo-style de novo assembly of Asian and African human genomes from short reads; assembly methodology, but reads are assembled rather than merged pairwise into longer fragments.

title: Meraculous: De Novo Genome Assembly with Short Paired-End Reads
reason: Meraculous assembles paired 75-bp reads through a k-mer graph and uses pairs for scaffolding and gap closure; paired-end assembly context, not a read merging tool.

title: FLASH Irradiation with Proton Beams: Beam Characteristics and Their Implications for Beam Diagnostics
reason: Concerns FLASH proton-beam radiotherapy dose rates and beam diagnostics; shares only the acronym FLASH and nothing about sequencing reads or assembly.

title: De novo finished 2.8 Mbp Staphylococcus aureus genome assembly from 100 bp short and long range paired-end reads
reason: Edena finishes a Staphylococcus aureus genome by exploiting paired-end insert distance in an overlaps graph; it uses pairing information inside an assembler rather than merging overlapping mates into longer reads.

title: Construction of a chromosome-scale long-read reference genome assembly for potato
reason: Chromosome-scale potato assembly from nanopore long reads and Hi-C scaffolding; a genome resource paper in the assembly area, unrelated to merging paired-end reads.

title: FLASH: fast length adjustment of short reads to improve genome assemblies.
reason: FLASH extends read length by overlapping and merging paired-end reads from short-fragment libraries and shows substantially greater contig and scaffold N50 when used before assembly; precisely the tool the question describes.

title: Racon - Rapid consensus module for raw de novo genome assembly of long uncorrected reads
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: Racon is a consensus module for raw de novo assembly of long uncorrected reads, which is assembly polishing rather than paired-end read merging.

title: Effect of sequence depth and length in long-read assembly of the maize inbred NC358
reason: Measures how PacBio depth and subread length affect maize long-read assembly contiguity; touches the general theme that longer reads help assembly but describes no merging tool for read pairs.

title: ScaffMatch: scaffolding algorithm based on maximum weight matching
reason: ScaffMatch scaffolds contigs using paired-end insert sizes via maximum weight matching; downstream scaffolding stage, not merging overlapping reads into longer fragments.

title: Efficient de novo assembly of highly heterozygous genomes from whole-genome shotgun short reads
reason: Platanus assembles heterozygous diploid genomes with optimized k-mer de Bruijn graphs and paired-end scaffolding; assembler for a different problem than read merging.

title: Illumina error correction near highly repetitive DNA regions improves de novo genome assembly
reason: BrownieCorrector corrects Illumina reads overlapping repetitive patterns to improve de novo assembly; a pre-assembly read processing tool, but it performs error correction rather than merging read pairs.

reason: Update on human DC subset ontogeny and transcription factor requirements; general background on dendritic cell biology with nothing on apoptotic cell receptors or cross-priming.

title: CD36, a signaling receptor and fatty acid transporter that regulates immune cell metabolism and fate
reason: Review of CD36 as signalling receptor and fatty acid transporter shaping macrophage and T cell metabolism and fate; receptor background, not DC engulfment of dying cells or cytotoxic T cell priming.

title: Mature dendritic cells use endocytic receptors to capture and present antigens
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Shows mature DCs still capture antigen by receptor-mediated endocytosis and phagocytosis and cross-present it on MHC class I, directly engaging the maturation-restricted, receptor-dependent capture-and-cross-present model.

title: RIPK1 and NF-κB signaling in dying cells determines cross-priming of CD8 + T cells
reason: Addresses cross-priming of CD8 T cells by DCs from necroptotic and apoptotic cells, showing RIPK1/NF-kB signalling in the dying cell is required; answers the dying-cell-to-CTL axis from the dying cell side.

title: Induction of human tumor-loaded dendritic cells.
reason: Photopheresis protocol generating CD36+ immature DCs that engulf apoptotic malignant T cells for vaccination; uptake is observed but the readouts are MHC II and alloproliferation, with no receptor blocking or CTL cross-presentation.

title: Consequences of Cell Death
reason: Immature DCs phagocytose apoptotic and necrotic tumour cells, with cross-presentation of antigen to CD8 T cells after apoptotic cell uptake plus a necrosis-derived maturation signal; covers uptake by immature DCs and class I cross-presentation.

title: Microparticles (Ectosomes) Shed by Stored Human Platelets Downregulate Macrophages and Modify the Development of Dendritic Cells
reason: Platelet-derived ectosomes bearing phosphatidylserine and CD36 modify macrophage and immature DC differentiation and reduce phagocytic activity; a different problem, sharing only PS/CD36 and immature DC vocabulary.

title: Clearing the Dead: Apoptotic Cell Sensing, Recognition, Engulfment, and Digestion
journal: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
reason: Review of apoptotic cell sensing, eat-me signals and their cognate receptors, engulfment and digestion by phagocytes; background on corpse recognition without DC-specific receptors or cross-presentation to CTLs.

title: The 5th edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours: Myeloid and Histiocytic/Dendritic Neoplasms
reason: WHO classification scheme for myeloid and histiocytic/dendritic neoplasms; a tumour nosology paper that shares only the word dendritic with the question.

title: Most lymphoid organ dendritic cell types are phenotypically and functionally immature
reason: Systematic assessment showing most lymphoid organ DCs are phenotypically and functionally immature and can still process newly encountered antigen; context on the immature state, not on dying-cell receptors or CTL cross-priming.

title: Morphologically and functionally intact dendritic cells can be derived from the peripheral blood of aged individuals
reason: Compares monocyte-derived DCs from aged and young donors for morphology, phenotype and tetanus toxoid presentation; DC antigen presentation in ageing is a different question from apoptotic cell engulfment via receptors.

title: Opsonization of apoptotic cells by autologous iC3b facilitates clearance by immature dendritic cells, down-regulates DR and CD86, and up-regulates CC chemokine receptor 7.
reason: Tests receptor-dependent clearance of apoptotic cells by immature DCs, using iC3b opsonization alongside the known alphavbeta3, alphavbeta5 and CD36 routes; receptor-mediated dying-cell uptake by immature DCs, with tolerogenic rather than CTL outcomes.

title: Dying cells actively regulate adaptive immune responses
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: dying cells actively regulating adaptive immune responses is the surrounding topic but the title names neither DC uptake receptors nor presentation to cytotoxic lymphocytes.

title: Uptake of apoptotic DC converts immature DC into tolerogenic DC that induce differentiation of Foxp3+ Treg
reason: Immature DCs that ingest apoptotic DCs become tolerogenic and induce Foxp3 Tregs via TGF-beta1; dying-cell uptake by immature DCs is shown, but no receptors are identified and the T cell outcome is regulatory, not cytotoxic.

title: Antithymocyte Globulins Suppress Dendritic Cell Function by Multiple Mechanisms
reason: Antithymocyte globulins bind many DC surface molecules including CD36 and inhibit endocytosis and T cell stimulation; a transplant immunosuppression study, not an account of apoptotic cell engulfment and cross-presentation.

title: Immature, Semi-Mature, and Fully Mature Dendritic Cells: Toward a DC-Cancer Cells Interface That Augments Anticancer Immunity
reason: Review of immature, semi-mature and fully mature DC states arising from interaction with dying cancer cells; concerns maturation phenotype and tolerogenicity rather than the uptake receptors or CTL cross-presentation.

title: A role for CD36 in the regulation of dendritic cell function
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Blocking antibodies against CD36 and CD51 (alphav), the receptors that mediate DC phagocytosis of apoptotic cells, modulate DC maturation and T cell activation; addresses both named receptors on DCs handling apoptotic cells, though the readout is DC function not CTL cross-priming.

title: Dendritic cell-based immunotherapy
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: a general dendritic cell-based immunotherapy piece, with nothing in the title on dying-cell uptake receptors or cross-presentation to cytotoxic lymphocytes.

title: Macrophages transfer antigens to dendritic cells by releasing exosomes containing dead‐cell‐associated antigens partially through a ceramide‐dependent pathway to enhance CD 4+ T‐cell responses
reason: Macrophages hand dead-cell-associated antigen to DCs through ceramide-dependent exosomes to boost CD4 T cell responses; concerns intercellular antigen transfer and CD4 priming, not DC surface receptors or cytotoxic T cell cross-presentation.

title: The Induction of Tolerance by Dendritic Cells That Have Captured Apoptotic Cells
reason: Review of tolerance induced by DCs that have captured apoptotic cells, focused on maturation as the control point; the DC-apoptotic cell axis is the setting but receptors and CTL cross-presentation are not what is addressed.

title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor contributes to the MEK/ERK-dependent maintenance of the immature state of human dendritic cells.
reason: MEK/ERK and AhR maintenance of the immature human DC state, including regulation of CD36 and other lipid-binding scavenger receptor genes; gene expression control rather than apoptotic cell engulfment and CTL priming.

title: The Fibronectin Domains of the Neural Adhesion Molecule TAX-1 Are Necessary and Sufficient for Homophilic Binding
reason: Maps which domains of the neural adhesion glycoprotein TAX-1 (Ig vs fibronectin type III) mediate homophilic binding, so it supplies the domain-architecture part of the question, but says nothing about alternative transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Structural variants of the neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM) in developing feathers.
reason: Reports two N-CAM transcripts differing by a 93-bp insert, glycosylation-based polypeptide variants and polysialic acid that lowers adhesion; that is alternative transcripts plus surface regulation of the molecule, though studied in skin/feather rather than nervous tissue.

title: Neural cell recognition molecule F11: Homology with fibronectin type III and immunoglobulin type C domains
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: the title states homology of the neural recognition molecule F11 with fibronectin type III and immunoglobulin C domains, which addresses the domain-architecture facet but not surface regulation or transcripts.

title: Expression of Neural Cell Adhesion Molecules in Normal and Pathologic Tissues
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
reason: Review of CAM expression patterns in normal and pathologic tissue; only mentions Ig-like domains in passing and never treats domain architecture, surface modulation or splice variants as its subject.

title: Structure of a new nervous system glycoprotein, Nr-CAM, and its relationship to subgroups of neural cell adhesion molecules.
reason: Titled structure of a new nervous system glycoprotein and delivers exactly the asked-for combination: six Ig-like domains plus five fibronectin type III repeats, transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, cDNA variants indicating alternative processing to several mRNAs, and cell-surface labelling on neurons.

title: L1-CAM and N-CAM: From Adhesion Proteins to Pharmacological Targets.
reason: Focused on L1/N-CAM signalling through growth factor receptors and their use as pharmacological and prognostic targets, not on domain layout, splice variants or surface modulation.

title: Immunoelectron microscopic localization of neural cell adhesion molecules (L1, N-CAM, and MAG) and their shared carbohydrate epitope and myelin basic protein in developing sciatic nerve.
reason: Immunoelectron microscopic localization of L1, N-CAM and MAG in developing sciatic nerve; a distribution study of the same molecules, with no analysis of domains, transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Polymer Adhesin Domains in Gram-Positive Cell Surface Proteins
reason: Concerns polymer adhesin domains in Gram-positive bacterial surface proteins binding DNA and lipoteichoic acid; a different subject that shares only the words adhesion and domain.

title: Several extracellular domains of the neural cell adhesion molecule L1 are involved in neurite outgrowth and cell body adhesion
reason: Dissects the extracellular Ig-like domains and fibronectin type III repeats of the neural adhesion glycoprotein L1 and assigns neurite outgrowth versus cell body adhesion to specific modules, answering the domain-architecture facet only.

title: The cytoplasmic domain of C-CAM is required for C-CAM-mediated adhesion function: studies of a C-CAM transcript containing an unspliced intron
reason: Shows an alternatively processed C-CAM transcript with an unspliced intron yielding a truncated cytoplasmic domain that loses adhesion function, addressing the transcript-variant and cytoplasmic-domain question for an Ig-superfamily CAM, but in hepatocyte and intestinal tissue rather than nervous system.

title: Myelin protein zero and membrane adhesion
reason: Reviews how myelin protein zero mediates membrane self-adhesion and disease mutations; a nervous system adhesion glycoprotein, but the topic is the adhesive lattice mechanism, not multidomain architecture, splice variants or surface modulation.

title: Proteoglycan form and function: A comprehensive nomenclature of proteoglycans
reason: A proteoglycan nomenclature paper classifying gene families by protein modules and noting spliced variants; different molecule class and no neural adhesion glycoprotein analysis, so only generic module/splicing overlap.

title: Developmental biology of a neural cell adhesion molecule
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: developmental biology of a neural cell adhesion molecule points to expression and development rather than the domain architecture, surface regulation and transcript variants asked about.

title: Adhesion among neural cells of the chick embryo. III. Relationship of the surface molecule CAM to cell adhesion and the development of histotypic patterns.
reason: Antibody-perturbation study of CAM in chick neural cell aggregation and histotypic pattern formation; notes changes in surface density with age but contains no domain, transcript or splicing analysis.

title: Regulation of neural cell adhesion molecule sialylation state
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: regulation of N-CAM sialylation state is directly the surface-regulation facet of the question for the relevant nervous system adhesion glycoprotein, though domains and transcripts are not indicated.

title: Glial cells express N-CAM/D2-CAM-like polypeptides in vitro
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: expression of N-CAM/D2-CAM-like polypeptides by glial cells in vitro is a cell-type expression finding, not domain architecture, surface modulation or splicing.

title: Cell Adhesion Molecules and Protein Synthesis Regulation in Neurons
reason: Reviews how CAM binding regulates neuronal transcription and translation; downstream signalling to protein synthesis is a different question from the molecule's own domain layout and transcript variants.

title: The neural cell adhesion molecule N-CAM enhances L1-dependent cell-cell interactions.
reason: Demonstrates cis-modulation at the cell surface, where N-CAM on the same membrane converts L1 into a more potent receptor complex; that is a genuine surface-regulation mechanism for these neural adhesion glycoproteins, but no domain mapping or transcripts.

title: Genetic deletion of a neural cell adhesion molecule variant (N-CAM-180) produces distinct defects in the central nervous system
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: genetic deletion of the N-CAM-180 variant tests the specific function of one alternatively spliced isoform of the nervous system adhesion glycoprotein, supplying part of the alternative-transcript answer.

title: High N-glycan multiplicity is critical for neuronal adhesion and sensitizes the developing cerebellum to N-glycosylation defect
reason: Srd5a3 cerebellar knockout study on N-glycan multiplicity and IgSF-CAM-mediated neurite outgrowth; glycosylation of neural CAMs is context, but the paper's subject is a congenital glycosylation defect, not the glycoprotein's domains, transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Characterization of multiple adhesive and counteradhesive domains in the extracellular matrix protein cytotactin.
reason: Maps adhesive and counteradhesive activities to fibronectin type III, fibrinogen and EGF-like domains of cytotactin, an extracellular matrix protein rather than a cell-surface neural adhesion glycoprotein, and covers neither transcripts nor surface modulation.

title: The response to injury in the peripheral nervous system
journal: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery - British Volume
reason: Clinical account of peripheral nerve injury outcome and connective-tissue sheath disruption; no adhesion glycoprotein, domain or transcript content at all.

title: Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule: Structure, Immunoglobulin-Like Domains, Cell Surface Modulation, and Alternative RNA Splicing
reason: Reports the complete N-CAM polypeptide sequences with five immunoglobulin-like extracellular domains, shows regulation occurs by cell surface modulation of affinity, prevalence, mobility and distribution, and identifies alternative RNA splicing generating different cytoplasmic domains; this is precisely the question.

title: Dynamic regulation of cell adhesion molecules during axon outgrowth
reason: Describes dynamic regulation of CAM function at the neuronal cell surface, including restriction of surface location and duration of membrane expression alongside transcriptional control, which answers the surface-regulation facet for neural adhesion molecules.

title: Different Domains of the F3 Neuronal Adhesion Molecule are Involved in Adhesion and Neurite Outgrowth Promotion
reason: Uses deletion constructs to assign adhesion to the fibronectin type III repeats and neurite outgrowth to other parts of the GPI-anchored neuronal adhesion glycoprotein F3, addressing domain architecture but not transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Immunoelectron microscopic localization of neural cell adhesion molecules (L1, N-CAM, and myelin-associated glycoprotein) in regenerating adult mouse sciatic nerve.
reason: Immunoelectron localization of L1, N-CAM and MAG during sciatic nerve regeneration; expression and distribution during regrowth, with no domain, splicing or surface-modulation analysis.

title: Molecular cloning and expression of a novel adhesion molecule, SC1
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: molecular cloning and expression of the novel adhesion molecule SC1 does not establish nervous system context or any treatment of domain architecture, surface regulation or alternative transcripts.

title: Neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM) accumulates in denervated and paralyzed skeletal muscles.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Shows N-CAM reappears in denervated and paralyzed skeletal muscle; regulation of expression level by innervation state in muscle, a different question from the glycoprotein's domain architecture and transcript variants.

title: Studies on the transmembrane disposition of the neural cell adhesion molecule N‐CAM
reason: Defines the transmembrane and cytoplasmic disposition of the 180, 140 and 120 kDa N-CAM forms, showing the 120 kDa chain may lack a membrane-spanning segment and that the larger forms are phosphorylated, so it supplies real domain-architecture information for the distinct forms.

title: Heparan Sulfate Chains from Glypican and Syndecans Bind the Hep II Domain of Fibronectin Similarly Despite Minor Structural Differences
reason: Compares heparan sulfate chains of glypican and syndecans binding the Hep II domain of fibronectin; a proteoglycan-fibronectin binding study unrelated to neural adhesion glycoprotein domains or transcripts.

title: The role of neutrophils in the dysfunction of central nervous system barriers
reason: Reviews neutrophil-driven damage to the blood-brain and blood-cerebrospinal fluid barriers in neuroinflammation; a different subject that shares only nervous system vocabulary.

title: Neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM) is required for cell type segregation and normal ultrastructure in pancreatic islets.
reason: N-CAM-deficient mice show loss of alpha cell segregation and altered ultrastructure in pancreatic islets; same molecule but the question addressed is islet organogenesis, not domains, surface modulation or transcripts.

title: Polysialic acid is associated with sodium channels and the neural cell adhesion molecule N-CAM in adult rat brain.
reason: Maps polysialic acid distribution in adult rat brain and shows sodium channel alpha subunits also carry it; the main finding concerns a second polySia carrier rather than regulation of the adhesion glycoprotein's surface activity, domains or transcripts.

title: Interactions of the chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan phosphacan, the extracellular domain of a receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase, with neurons, glia, and neural cell adhesion molecules.
reason: Characterizes binding of the proteoglycan phosphacan to N-CAM and Ng-CAM and its inhibition of adhesion; a heterophilic ligand study, not an account of the CAM's own domain architecture, splice variants or surface modulation.

title: Two adhesive systems cooperatively regulate axon ensheathment and myelin growth in the CNS
reason: Shows paranodal and internodal adhesion systems cooperate in axon ensheathment and myelin wrapping; functional myelin biology rather than the domain architecture, surface regulation or transcripts of an adhesion glycoprotein.

title: Elucidation of the molecular actions of NCAM and structurally related cell adhesion molecules
reason: Reviews NCAM and its relatives as glycoproteins sharing immunoglobulin and fibronectin type III motifs and grouped by the number of each domain type, so it supplies the domain-architecture framework, though splicing and surface modulation are not its focus.

title: The neuronal chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan neurocan binds to the neural cell adhesion molecules Ng-CAM/L1/NILE and N-CAM, and inhibits neuronal adhesion and neurite outgrowth.
reason: Shows the proteoglycan neurocan binds Ng-CAM/L1 and N-CAM and inhibits neurite outgrowth; an external ligand interaction study, not the CAM's domain layout, transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Activity of neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM) components: a review.
reason: Review of N-CAM components stating that different forms arise by alternative splicing of one gene and that carbohydrate amount sets binding strength; both transcript and surface-carbohydrate regulation facets appear, but the focus shifts to brain injury and reorganization.

title: Sequence of a cDNA clone encoding the polysialic acid-rich and cytoplasmic domains of the neural cell adhesion molecule N-CAM.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Sequences the cDNA covering the polysialic acid-rich and cytoplasmic domains of N-CAM, reports Ig-superfamily repeats and the membrane-spanning segment, attributes the large and small cytoplasmic domain polypeptides to alternative splicing of one gene, and links those domains to cell-surface modulation.

title: Binding of neural cell adhesion molecules (N-CAMs) to the cellular prion protein
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: binding of N-CAMs to the cellular prion protein is a heterophilic partner finding, not the domain architecture, surface regulation or transcripts asked about.

title: Heterophilic interactions of the neural cell adhesion molecules Ng-CAM and Nr-CAM with neural receptors and extracellular matrix proteins
reason: Summarizes heterophilic partners of Ng-CAM and Nr-CAM and their roles in axon growth and guidance; binding partnerships and localization rather than domain architecture, splice variants or surface modulation.

title: The 180-kD component of the neural cell adhesion molecule N-CAM is involved in cell-cell contacts and cytoskeleton-membrane interactions
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: the 180-kD N-CAM component is the large-cytoplasmic-domain splice product, and its involvement in cell-cell contacts and cytoskeleton-membrane interaction is exactly the isoform-specific surface behaviour the question covers.

title: Specification of synaptic connectivity by cell surface interactions
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: specification of synaptic connectivity by cell surface interactions is broad wiring context, with no indication of domain architecture, surface modulation or transcript variants.

title: Mice Lacking Sodium Channel β1 Subunits Display Defects in Neuronal Excitability, Sodium Channel Expression, and Nodal Architecture
reason: Sodium channel beta1 knockout mice studied for excitability, channel expression and nodal architecture; beta1 is an Ig-domain surface glycoprotein with adhesive properties, but the paper's subject is channel and node function, not domains, splicing or surface modulation.

title: Identity of Leu-19 (CD56) leukocyte differentiation antigen and neural cell adhesion molecule.
reason: Establishes that the Leu-19/CD56 leukocyte antigen is structurally the same 140 kDa sialylated N-CAM polypeptide; identity and tissue distribution on hematopoietic cells rather than domain architecture, splice variants or surface regulation.

title: Neural cell-cell and cell-substrate adhesion through N-cadherin, N-CAM and L1.
reason: Immobilizes N-cadherin, N-CAM and L1 proteins and antibodies on coated glass and measures neuron adhesion by impedance sensing; a substrate engineering and blocking study, not molecular domain, transcript or surface-modulation analysis.

title: Families of neural cell adhesion molecules
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: families of neural cell adhesion molecules signals a general family overview, useful background but with no stated treatment of domain architecture, surface regulation or alternative transcripts.

title: Neural cell adhesion molecule mediates initial interactions between spinal cord neurons and muscle cells in culture.
reason: Fab' blocking experiments showing N-CAM mediates initial spinal cord neuron to myotube adhesion; a function-in-culture study without domain mapping, splicing or surface modulation.

title: A heparin-binding domain from N-CAM is involved in neural cell-substratum adhesion.
reason: Identifies a 25 kDa heparin-binding domain within N-CAM by limited proteolysis and shows the molecule is multifunctional with separate cell- and heparin-binding domains, which addresses the domain-architecture facet for this nervous system adhesion glycoprotein.

title: Identification of a novel contactin‐associated transmembrane receptor with multiple domains implicated in protein–protein interactions
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: identification of a contactin-associated transmembrane receptor with multiple domains implicated in protein-protein interactions is a domain-architecture report for a neural cell-surface adhesion-related glycoprotein.

title: The ubiquitous neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM).
reason: Review noting four main N-CAM isoforms plus many variants from alternative splicing and post-translational modification including PSA, which addresses the transcript and surface-modification facets, although much of it turns to gut motility and tumours.

title: Two forms of 1B236/myelin-associated glycoprotein, a cell adhesion molecule for postnatal neural development, are produced by alternative splicing.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Shows two forms of the myelin-associated glycoprotein cell adhesion molecule arise as alternative splice products of one gene, differing in their C-terminal cytoplasmic structures, on an N terminus of five immunoglobulin-like domains; domain architecture plus alternative transcripts of a nervous system adhesion glycoprotein.

title: Binding properties of a cell adhesion molecule from neural tissue.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Tests binding of purified N-CAM in lipid vesicles to cells to support a homophilic ligand mechanism; a binding-property study with no domain, transcript or surface-modulation content.

title: Cellular signaling by neural cell adhesion molecules of the immunoglobulin superfamily
reason: Review of intracellular signalling triggered by N-CAM and L1 binding, with emphasis on neurite outgrowth and gene expression assays; signalling consequences rather than domain architecture, splicing or surface modulation of the glycoprotein.

title: Sticky Signaling—Adhesion Class G Protein–Coupled Receptors Take the Stage
reason: Discusses the hybrid architecture and autoproteolytic NTF/CTF fragments of adhesion class G protein-coupled receptors; domain-layout discussion but for a distinct receptor family, not a nervous system adhesion glycoprotein with splice variants.

title: Neural adhesion molecule L1 as a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily with binding domains similar to fibronectin
reason: No abstract, graded on title alone: the title places the neural adhesion molecule L1 in the immunoglobulin superfamily with fibronectin-like binding domains, which is the domain-architecture facet for a nervous system adhesion glycoprotein.

title: Molecular Aspects of Thyroid Hormone Actions
reason: Comprehensive review of thyroid hormone receptor isoforms and genomic and nongenomic hormone action; an entirely different subject from neural adhesion glycoprotein structure.

title: L-selectin: A Major Regulator of Leukocyte Adhesion, Migration and Signaling
reason: Reviews L-selectin domains, cytoplasmic tail signalling and ectodomain shedding in leukocyte adhesion; comparable structural and surface-regulation themes but for an immune adhesion receptor, not a nervous system adhesion glycoprotein.

title: Cadherins in development: cell adhesion, sorting, and tissue morphogenesis
reason: Reviews the cadherin family, its extracellular repeats and regulation of adhesion during morphogenesis; a different adhesion protein family and no treatment of neural glycoprotein transcripts or surface modulation.

title: Effects of altered expression of the neural cell adhesion molecule, N-CAM, on early neural development in Xenopus embryos.
reason: Misexpresses synthetic N-CAM transcripts in Xenopus embryos to test whether N-CAM regulates neural tube formation; an in vivo function test rather than an account of domain architecture, surface modulation or splice variants.

title: Neural GPI anchored cell adhesion molecules
reason: Review of GPI-anchored neural CAMs covering expression, protein interactions and GPI-linked signalling; membrane anchoring is touched on but the domain architecture, splicing and surface-modulation questions are not its subject.

title: Characterization of chemokines and their receptors in the central nervous system: physiopathological implications
reason: Characterizes chemokines and chemokine receptors in the central nervous system and their pathological roles; a different molecular system with no adhesion glycoprotein domain or transcript content.

title: Cell surface modulation of the neural cell adhesion molecule resulting from alternative mRNA splicing in a tissue-specific developmental sequence.
reason: Directly titled cell surface modulation of the neural cell adhesion molecule resulting from alternative mRNA splicing, and shows the ld-specific 783-bp exon, tissue-specific ld/sd transcript use and the resulting cytoplasmic-domain difference in surface expression.

title: To Stick or Not to Stick: The Multiple Roles of Cell Adhesion Molecules in Neural Circuit Assembly
reason: Reviews adhesive and non-adhesive roles of CAMs in axon guidance, fasciculation and circuit refinement; functional circuit assembly rather than domain architecture, surface regulation or transcript variants.

title: Adhesion Molecules in the Nervous System: Structural Insights into Function and Diversity
reason: Reviews structural mechanisms of adhesive binding across nervous system adhesion molecule families and highlights precisely regulated alternative splicing as a diversification mechanism, covering the structural and transcript facets at family level rather than for one glycoprotein.

title: Structure of the chicken neuron-glia cell adhesion molecule, Ng-CAM: origin of the polypeptides and relation to the Ig superfamily.
reason: Reports the Ng-CAM architecture of six immunoglobulin-like domains, five fibronectin type III repeats, transmembrane and cytoplasmic segments, and traces its multiple polypeptides to proteolytic cleavage of a single gene product rather than to alternative transcripts.

title: Differential contributions of Ng-CAM and N-CAM to cell adhesion in different neural regions.
reason: Attributes the differing contributions of Ng-CAM and N-CAM in brain, ganglia and retina to prevalence and polarity modulation with measured Ng-CAM/N-CAM surface ratios, which is the surface-regulation facet, though domains and transcripts are absent.

title: Influenza A Virus Lacking the NS1 Gene Replicates in Interferon-Deficient Systems
reason: delNS1 reverse-genetics study of influenza A NS1; abstract frames NS1 as the only nonstructural protein with several regulatory functions and demonstrates its interferon-antagonist role, supplying a real part of the answer rather than the full range of roles.

title: The 58-kilodalton inhibitor of the interferon-induced double-stranded RNA-activated protein kinase is a tetratricopeptide repeat protein with oncogenic properties.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Subject is the cellular PKR inhibitor p58 and its oncogenic TPR properties; influenza appears only as the stimulus that activates p58, so it is background on a host factor, not on NS1's roles.

title: Cryo-EM structure of Influenza A virus NS1 and antiviral protein kinase PKR complex.
reason: Cryo-EM structure of the influenza A NS1-PKR complex; explicitly calls NS1 an exceedingly multifunctional virulence component and details one of its roles (PKR antagonism, innate immune evasion) at residue level.

title: Essential Role for the dsRNA-Dependent Protein Kinase PKR in Innate Immunity to Viral Infection
reason: PKR-knockout mouse study on innate immunity to VSV and influenza; it characterises the host kinase NS1 targets and never addresses the functions of the viral nonstructural protein itself.

title: A site on the influenza A virus NS1 protein mediates both inhibition of PKR activation and temporal regulation of viral RNA synthesis
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: a single NS1 site mediating both PKR inhibition and temporal regulation of viral RNA synthesis shows two distinct influenza A NS1 activities, a real part of the multifunctionality asked about.

title: The Central Role of Non-Structural Protein 1 (NS1) in Influenza Biology and Infection
reason: Review whose stated purpose is the structure, dynamics, multiple functions and interactions of influenza NS1 and its central role in viral biology; exactly the many-roles question asked.

title: Molecular Evolution of the Influenza A Virus Non-structural Protein 1 in Interspecies Transmission and Adaptation
reason: Review of influenza A NS1 evolution that discusses two of its functions (CPSF4-mediated host shutoff and interferon suppression) and its plastic, multifunctional nature, but frames them around interspecies adaptation rather than cataloguing all roles.

title: Mini Review: A Glimpse of Nonstructural Protein 1 of Influenza a H1N1
reason: Mini review dedicated to influenza A NS1, describing its RBD and effector domains and its multifunctional nature across immune evasion, PI3K activation, PKR inhibition and mRNA nuclear export block.

title: Influenza A Virus Nucleoprotein Exploits Hsp40 to Inhibit PKR Activation
reason: Shows influenza nucleoprotein, not NS1, exploits Hsp40 to inhibit PKR; same virus and same pathway but a different viral protein, so it is context rather than an answer about the nonstructural protein.

title: NS5A domain I antagonises PKR to facilitate the assembly of infectious hepatitis C virus particles
reason: Hepatitis C NS5A domain I antagonising PKR to allow particle assembly; an analogous multifunctional nonstructural protein but of a different virus, so useful comparative background only.

title: Incorporation of pseudouridine into mRNA enhances translation by diminishing PKR activation
reason: Pseudouridine-modified in vitro transcribed mRNA and reduced PKR activation; an mRNA-therapeutics translation study with no influenza virus or nonstructural protein content, sharing only PKR vocabulary.

title: Mutant Influenza Viruses with a Defective NS1 Protein Cannot Block the Activation of PKR in Infected Cells
reason: Temperature-sensitive NS1 mutant viruses tie NS1 RNA binding to blocking PKR autophosphorylation and to viral protein synthesis, documenting two coupled NS1 activities in infected cells.

title: Conformational plasticity of the influenza A virus NS1 protein
reason: Review of influenza A NS1 conformational plasticity that explicitly argues the protein's multiple activities depend on its quaternary dynamics; addresses NS1 multifunctionality but from a structural-plasticity angle.

title: Host Immune Response to Influenza A Virus Infection
reason: Broad review of innate and adaptive host immune responses to influenza A, mentioning viral escape only generically; provides the host-side context without covering the nonstructural protein's roles.

title: NS1-Binding Protein (NS1-BP): a Novel Human Protein That Interacts with the Influenza A Virus Nonstructural NS1 Protein Is Relocalized in the Nuclei of Infected Cells
reason: Identifies the host NS1-binding protein NS1-BP and links NS1 to inhibition of pre-mRNA splicing, giving a concrete non-interferon function of the influenza A nonstructural protein.

title: MAP kinase‐activated protein kinases 2 and 3 are required for influenza A virus propagation and act via inhibition of PKR
reason: Host kinases MK2 and MK3 recruit p58IPK/p88rIPK to shut off PKR during influenza infection; the mechanism described is host-protein driven and NS1 is not the subject.

title: Immunomodulatory Nonstructural Proteins of Influenza A Viruses
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: a review of immunomodulatory nonstructural proteins of influenza A viruses covers the immune-evasion subset of the roles asked about, but the title limits it to immunomodulation.

title: Influenza A Virus Virulence Depends on Two Amino Acids in the N-Terminal Domain of Its NS1 Protein To Facilitate Inhibition of the RNA-Dependent Protein Kinase PKR
reason: Mutational study of NS1 arginines 35 and 46 showing PKR binding is indispensable for propagation and virulence in PKR-/- mice; describes NS1 as pleiotropic and pins down one key function.

title: Biochemical and Genetic Evidence for Complex Formation Between the Influenza A Virus NS1 Protein and the Interferon-induced PKR Protein Kinase
reason: Biochemical and genetic demonstration of an NS1-PKR complex and mapping of the binding site, establishing a specific mechanistic role of influenza A NS1 in PKR modulation.

title: Roles of the Non-Structural Proteins of Influenza A Virus
reason: Review titled Roles of the Non-Structural Proteins of Influenza A Virus, covering NS1, PB1-F2 and PA-X and their versatile functions in replication, immune evasion, apoptosis and pathogenicity; directly the question asked.

title: Old and New Functions for the Adenovirus Virus-Associated RNAs
reason: Adenovirus VA RNAI/RNAII noncoding RNAs and their multifunctional suppression of PKR and RNAi; a different virus and a non-protein factor, overlapping only in PKR and multifunctionality wording.

title: NPM1/B23: A Multifunctional Chaperone in Ribosome Biogenesis and Chromatin Remodeling
reason: NPM1/B23 as a multifunctional cellular chaperone in ribosome biogenesis, chromatin remodeling and tumour development; no virus and no nonstructural protein, only the word multifunctional in common.

title: Viperin: A Multifunctional, Interferon-Inducible Protein that Regulates Virus Replication
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: viperin is an interferon-inducible host restriction factor, not a viral nonstructural protein, so the shared term multifunctional does not make it relevant.

title: Large-scale analysis of influenza A virus sequences reveals potential drug target sites of non-structural proteins
reason: Sequence conservation analysis of influenza NS1 and NS2 to nominate drug target residues; concerns the right proteins but answers a druggability question, not what functions they perform.

title: Robust expression of vault RNAs induced by influenza A virus plays a critical role in suppression of PKR-mediated innate immunity
reason: Shows NS1 is the inducer of vault RNAs and that vtRNA upregulation is required for efficient NS1-mediated PKR suppression, so it dissects the mechanism behind an NS1 function during influenza infection.
