title: Metabolic Regulation of Stem Cells in Aging
reason: Review of nutrient sensing and dietary restriction in stem cell aging; nutrient-sensing signaling is loosely adjacent background but nothing on mitochondrial fission or a fission-driving kinase.

title: AMPK is a mechano-metabolic sensor linking cell adhesion and mitochondrial dynamics to Myosin-dependent cell migration
reason: Reports that low adhesion lowers ATP/AMP to activate AMPK, and high AMPK activity induces mitochondrial fission during amoeboid migration; AMPK-driven fission demonstrated, with cell migration rather than fuel scarcity as the framing question.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Mitochondrial Quality Control in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
reason: Review of mitochondrial quality control (mitophagy, dynamics, biogenesis) in ischemic cardiomyopathy; same general area of mitochondrial dynamics but no energy-sensing kinase driving fission.

title: Regulation of mitochondrial functions by protein phosphorylation and dephosphorylation
reason: General review of mitochondria-localized kinases and phosphatases regulating mitochondrial function; useful background on mitochondrial phosphorylation without addressing fission on fuel depletion.

title: Melatonin alleviates rheumatoid arthritis via elimination of damaged mitochondria.
reason: Melatonin relieving rheumatoid arthritis by promoting mitophagy and limiting NLRP3 inflammasome; mitochondrial quality control context only, with MFF and AMPK appearing solely in the abbreviation list.

title: AMPK phosphorylation by Ssp1 is required for proper sexual differentiation in fission yeast
reason: AMPK (Ssp2) phosphorylation by Ssp1 governing nitrogen-starvation mitotic entry and sexual differentiation in fission yeast; energy-sensing kinase under starvation but the question studied is cell differentiation, and 'fission' here refers to the yeast, not mitochondria.

title: The peroxisome: an update on mysteries 2.0
reason: Peroxisome review covering membrane dynamics and division of that organelle; shares organelle division machinery as background but not mitochondrial fission or energy-sensing kinase control.

title: Distinct fission signatures predict mitochondrial degradation or biogenesis
reason: Title only (no abstract): distinct fission signatures predicting mitochondrial degradation or biogenesis is fission-subtype biology with no kinase or energy-scarcity element indicated.

title: Mitochondria orchestrate macrophage effector functions in atherosclerosis
reason: Title only (no abstract): mitochondria in macrophage effector functions in atherosclerosis is immunometabolism background, not kinase-driven mitochondrial division.

title: Adenylate kinase phosphotransfer communicates cellular energetic signals to ATP-sensitive potassium channels
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Adenylate kinase phosphotransfer relaying cellular energetic signals to KATP channels; energy-sensing signal transduction background, but the target is membrane excitability rather than mitochondrial division.

title: Mitochondrial Biogenesis through Activation of Nuclear Signaling Proteins
journal: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
reason: Review of transcriptional and signaling control of mitochondrial biogenesis; addresses mitochondrial mass and bioenergetics, not fission driven by an energy-sensing kinase.

title: A receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor, Tyrphostin A9 induces cancer cell death through Drp1 dependent mitochondria fragmentation
reason: Title only (no abstract): Tyrphostin A9 causing Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fragmentation and cancer cell death is drug-induced fission, with no energy-sensing kinase or fuel depletion.

title: Ensuring Adequate Energy Supply
reason: Short synopsis stating that mitotic kinases converge on mitochondria to promote fission and equal distribution in dividing cells; kinase-driven fission but the trigger is mitosis, not scarce fuel.

title: TFAM promotes mitochondrial division by increasing mitochondrial Sirt3.
reason: Demonstrates TFAM-Sirt3 promoting mitochondrial division through activation of the AMPK/MFF/Drp1 pathway, with AMPK inhibition and MFF depletion blocking fission; supports AMPK-driven fission although the trigger studied is TFAM, not energy scarcity.

title: Muscle-generated BDNF (brain derived neurotrophic factor) maintains mitochondrial quality control in female mice.
reason: Reports BDNF driving mitochondrial fission and mitophagy in skeletal muscle via PRKAA/AMPK-DNM1L/DRP1-MFF pathways; provides in vivo evidence for the AMPK-MFF fission axis, but in high-fat-diet lipid excess rather than fuel scarcity.

title: SUMOylation of MFF coordinates fission complexes to promote stress-induced mitochondrial fragmentation.
reason: Builds directly on AMPK phosphorylation of MFF being necessary for stress-induced mitochondrial fragmentation and adds SUMOylation of MFF at Lys151 regulating MiD binding; supplies mechanistic detail of the bioenergetic-stress fission complex.

title: During autophagy mitochondria elongate, are spared from degradation and sustain cell viability
reason: Title only (no abstract): mitochondria elongating and escaping degradation during autophagy concerns mitochondrial morphology under nutrient stress but reports elongation and names no energy-sensing kinase.

title: Pestiviruses utilize pyrimidine metabolism to regulate mitophagy for viral replication.
reason: DHODH and pyrimidine metabolism regulating mitophagy for pestivirus replication; a virology/metabolism question where MFF and AMPK appear only in the abbreviation list.

title: Keeping the home fires burning: AMP-activated protein kinase
journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Primer-style review of AMPK as the cellular energy sensor restoring ATP balance, including glucose sensing and biogenesis; strong background on the kinase but no mitochondrial fission finding.

title: Mir221- and Mir222 -enriched adsc-exosomes mitigate PM exposure-exacerbated cardiac ischemia-reperfusion injury through the modulation of the BNIP3-MAP1LC3B-BBC3/PUMA pathway
reason: Mir221/Mir222 exosomes mitigating particulate-matter-aggravated cardiac ischemia-reperfusion injury via BNIP3-LC3-PUMA; fission proteins DRP1 and MFF are only measured markers, with no energy-sensing kinase mechanism.

title: Mitochondrial Reactive Oxygen Species Dysregulation in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Fraction of the Whole
reason: Review of mitochondrial ROS dysregulation in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; mitochondrial dysfunction background with no fission or energy-sensing kinase content.

title: Mechanical force induces mitochondrial fission
reason: Mechanical force triggers mitochondrial fission with MFF proposed as a membrane-bound force sensor; same fission receptor but a mechanical, not metabolic, stimulus.

title: Faraway, so close! Functions of Endoplasmic reticulum–Endosome contacts
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids
reason: Title only (no abstract): functions of endoplasmic reticulum-endosome contact sites is a different organelle system entirely, with no mitochondrial fission or energy-sensing kinase connection.

title: Glucose starvation induces mitochondrial fragmentation depending on the dynamin GTPase Dnm1/Drp1 in fission yeast
reason: Glucose starvation induces rapid Dnm1/Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fragmentation in fission yeast, with PKA activity controlling the response and AMPK explicitly found not to be involved; addresses fuel-scarcity-driven mitochondrial division in a related organism with contrary evidence on the kinase.

title: Blocking exosomal secretion aggravates 1,4-benzoquinone-induced mitochondrial fission activated by the AMPK/MFF/Drp1 pathway in HL-60 cells.
reason: 1,4-benzoquinone lowers ATP and mediates mitochondrial fission through the AMPK/MFF/Drp1 pathway in HL-60 cells; the asked mechanism shown for a toxicant-induced condition, with exosomal secretion as the paper's focus.

title: Calcium signals tune AMPK activity and mitochondrial homeostasis in dendrites of developing neurons
reason: Calcium-CaMKK2 tuned AMPK activity phosphorylates MFF and ULK1 to initiate mitochondrial fission and mitophagy in growing dendrites; direct evidence for AMPK-driven fission, with calcium/activity rather than fuel depletion as the trigger.

title: Mff is an essential factor for mitochondrial recruitment of Drp1 during mitochondrial fission in mammalian cells
reason: Establishes Mff as the essential receptor recruiting Drp1 for mitochondrial fission, independent of Fis1; core fission machinery paper with no energy-sensing or nutrient-scarcity component.

title: AMP-activated protein kinase: the current landscape for drug development
reason: Title only (no abstract): AMPK drug development landscape is pharmacology background on the energy-sensing kinase without any mitochondrial fission content.

title: AMPK Promotes Autophagy by Facilitating Mitochondrial Fission
reason: Title only (no abstract), but the title states the asked finding outright: AMPK, the cellular energy-sensing kinase, promotes autophagy by facilitating mitochondrial fission.

title: Mitophagy and Ubiquitination Coordinate Context‐Specific Mitochondrial Quality Control and EMT/MET Plasticity to Drive Cancer Cell Invasion
reason: Review of mitophagy and ubiquitination in mitochondrial quality control and EMT/MET plasticity during cancer invasion; fission-fusion dynamics mentioned as one axis, no energy-sensing kinase driving division.

title: The SnRK1 Kinase as Central Mediator of Energy Signaling between Different Organelles
reason: One-line summary of plant SnRK1, the AMPK counterpart, as an integrator of energy signaling across organelles and hormone metabolism; related energy-sensing kinase but nothing on mitochondrial division.

title: AMPK activation promotes lipid droplet dispersion on detyrosinated microtubules to increase mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation
reason: AMPK activation during nutrient starvation disperses lipid droplets on detyrosinated microtubules to raise mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation; correct kinase and scarcity trigger, but the outcome is lipid droplet trafficking and beta-oxidation, not fission.

title: mTORC2–NDRG1–CDC42 axis couples fasting to mitochondrial fission
reason: Shows fasting activates mTORC2, whose phosphorylation of NDRG1 sustains mitochondrial fission via CDC42; answers the question of a nutrient-responsive kinase coupling fuel scarcity to mitochondrial division, for a different kinase than the energy sensor AMPK.

title: AMP-activated protein kinase – not just an energy sensor
reason: AMPK review on nucleotide and glucose sensing, the ADaM site and activators; notes only in passing that newer AMPK targets have roles in mitochondrial fission, so it is background rather than the finding.

title: Mitochondrial-derived vesicles drive budding-type fission of damaged lysosomes.
reason: Mitochondrial-derived vesicles deliver MFF to damaged lysosomes for DRP1-driven budding fission, promoted by AMPK activation; same kinase and fission adaptor applied to lysosomal, not mitochondrial, division.

title: AMPK activation induces mitophagy and promotes mitochondrial fission while activating TBK1 in a PINK1‐Parkin independent manner
reason: Shows AMPK activation by 991 promotes mitochondrial fission through MFF phosphorylation and induces mitophagy independent of PINK1-Parkin in muscle cells; strong support for AMPK-driven fission, obtained by pharmacological activation rather than fuel deprivation.

title: Evidence for Cross-species Influenza A Virus Transmission Within Swine Farms, China: A One Health, Prospective Cohort Study
reason: Prospective One Health cohort finds swine-lineage H1N1/H3N2 in pig farms and human ILI isolates nearly identical to the swine viruses, supplying real evidence of pig-to-people influenza crossing, though not the emergence of a new pandemic strain.

title: Detection in 2009 of the Swine Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Virus by a Subtyping Microarray
reason: The paper's own contribution is a subtyping microarray for detecting the 2009 swine-origin H1N1; the emergence and reassortant origins appear only as framing background, so it is a method paper on the same virus.

title: Advances and insights in the diagnosis of viral infections
reason: General review of viral diagnostic technologies across pandemics, SARS-CoV-2, HIV and influenza; shares only generic virology vocabulary and says nothing about a swine-origin virus appearing in humans.

title: Molecular epidemiology of novel swine origin influenza virus (S-OIV) from Gwalior, India, 2009.
reason: Molecular epidemiology of confirmed human swine-origin H1N1 cases in Gwalior, India, with HA sequencing and lineage assignment; documents the new pig-origin virus in people for one country rather than its initial emergence.

title: 2009 Swine-Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Resembles Previous Influenza Isolates
reason: Compares the 2009 swine-origin H1N1 with earlier swine H1N1 isolates and an earlier sequenced human case in Thailand, addressing where the new human-infecting swine virus came from and why it spreads in people.

title: Human influenza A viruses in pigs: Isolation of a H3N2 strain antigenically related to A/England/42/72 and evidence for continuous circulation of human viruses in the pig population
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title reports human H3N2 viruses isolated from pigs and continuous circulation of human viruses in swine, which is the reverse direction (human to pig), so only background on the interface.

title: Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 Virus among Healthy Show Pigs, United States
reason: Reports the pandemic A(H1N1)pdm09 virus found in healthy US show pigs after it had emerged in humans; concerns spread into pigs and the show interface, not the appearance of a pig virus in people.

title: Sensitivity of Rapid Influenza Diagnostic Testing for Swine-Origin 2009 A (H1N1) Influenza Virus in Children
reason: Diagnostic accuracy study of rapid influenza tests and DFA versus RT-PCR for swine-origin H1N1 in children; same virus but the question asked is test sensitivity, not how the virus appeared in humans.

title: Rapid-Test Sensitivity for Novel Swine-Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Virus in Humans
reason: Correspondence on rapid-test sensitivity for the novel swine-origin H1N1 in surveillance populations; the subject is assay performance, with the first human cases mentioned only as context.

title: Influenza A Viruses in the Swine Population: Ecology and Geographical Distribution
reason: Large literature review explicitly covering zoonotic spread of swine influenza A viruses to humans, their circulation in swine worldwide and interspecies transmission, so it supplies a substantial part of the answer.

title: Implications of the Emergence of a Novel H1 Influenza Virus
reason: Editorial on the emergence of a novel H1 influenza virus, describing the two reports of swine influenza virus transmission to humans and the reassortant swine-origin H1N1 now spreading among people.

title: Subclinical Influenza Virus A Infections in Pigs Exhibited at Agricultural Fairs, Ohio, USA, 2009–2011
reason: Surveillance of subclinical influenza A in pigs at Ohio agricultural fairs; isolates matched swine herd viruses and human risk is only inferred, with no human infection reported.

title: Antigenic and Genetic Characteristics of Swine-Origin 2009 A(H1N1) Influenza Viruses Circulating in Humans
reason: Antigenic and genetic characterization of the 2009 swine-origin A(H1N1) viruses circulating in humans, with the phylogenetic reconstruction of how the avian, swine and human gene segments assembled before emergence.

title: Complete Genome Sequence of a Novel H4N1 Influenza Virus Isolated from a Pig in Central China
reason: Genome sequence of a novel H4N1 virus isolated from a pig in China, described as wholly avian in origin; no human infection, so it is background on novel swine viruses and mixing-vessel concern.

title: In vitro and in vivo characterization of new swine-origin H1N1 influenza viruses
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title indicates in vitro and in vivo characterization of the new swine-origin H1N1 viruses, i.e. replication and pathogenicity work rather than their appearance in people.

title: Introduction of a Novel Swine-Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Virus into Milwaukee, Wisconsin in 2009
reason: Documents the introduction of the novel swine-origin H1N1 into a human population in southeastern Wisconsin with 679 confirmed human cases and displacement of seasonal subtypes, a real local account of the new virus appearing in people.

title: Molecular events leading to the creation of a pandemic influenza virus
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title addresses the molecular events creating a pandemic influenza virus, which speaks to the reassortment genesis of such a virus, though the specific pandemic and the human-appearance angle are unstated.

title: The origin of the recent swine influenza A(H1N1) virus infecting humans
reason: Title and abstract are precisely about the origin of the recent swine influenza A(H1N1) virus infecting humans, reporting that all genome segments are closest to common swine influenza viruses.

title: Anti-viral properties and mode of action of standardized Echinacea purpurea extract against highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1, H7N7) and swine-origin H1N1 (S-OIV).
reason: Tests an Echinacea purpurea extract for antiviral activity against H5N1, H7N7 and swine-origin H1N1; the subject is herbal antiviral inhibition, only sharing the virus with the question.

title: Origins and evolutionary genomics of the 2009 swine-origin H1N1 influenza A epidemic.
reason: Evolutionary genomic analysis of the 2009 swine-origin H1N1 origins, showing derivation from several swine-circulating viruses and dating the initial transmission to humans months before the outbreak was recognized.

title: Human Infection with Eurasian Avian-Like Swine Influenza A(H1N1) Virus, the Netherlands, September 2019
reason: Reports a zoonotic human infection of a pig farmer […] also found in his pigs, with antigenic and genetic characterization: a documented pig-origin virus appearing in a person.

title: Introductions and Evolution of Human-Origin Seasonal Influenza A Viruses in Multinational Swine Populations
reason: Its findings concern 20 introductions of human seasonal influenza viruses into swine and their persistence, the human-to-pig direction; useful interface background but not appearance of a swine virus in people.

title: A Simple Method for Molecular Detection of Swine-Origin and Human-Origin Influenza A Virus
reason: Presents a real-time RT-PCR SYBR Green screening assay and probes distinguishing seasonal from swine-origin influenza A; a detection method paper, not an account of the virus emerging in humans.

title: Emergence and pandemic potential of swine-origin H1N1 influenza virus
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title states the subject is the emergence and pandemic potential of swine-origin H1N1 influenza virus, exactly the appearance of a new pig-origin virus in the human population.

title: The pig as a mixing vessel for influenza viruses: Human and veterinary implications
journal: Journal of Molecular and Genetic Medicine
reason: Reviews pigs as a reassortment mixing vessel and cites novel reassortant swine viruses such as H2N3 that have been transmitted to humans, supplying the mechanistic part of how new pig-origin viruses reach people.

title: Prevention and Control of Influenza Viruses
reason: Chapter on prevention and control of influenza: biosecurity, poultry vaccination strategies, antivirals and universal vaccine candidates. A control and prophylaxis subject with no treatment of swine-to-human emergence.

title: Cytokine profiles induced by the novel swine-origin influenza A/H1N1 virus: implications for treatment strategies.
reason: Measures cytokine and mRNA profiles in macrophages infected with swine-origin H1N1 versus H5N1 to guide immunomodulator treatment; same virus but the question is host response and therapy.

title: The First Influenza Pandemic of the 21st Century
reason: Commentary on the second wave of the 2009 A(H1N1) pandemic, vaccine impact, antiviral resistance and ICU capacity; concerns pandemic management rather than the swine origin or first appearance in humans.

title: Characteristics of human infection with avian influenza viruses and development of new antiviral agents
reason: Reviews human infections with avian influenza viruses (H5N1, H7N9) and antiviral development; adjacent zoonotic-influenza background but the source species is birds, not pigs, and the focus is drugs.

title: Swine-origin influenza A (H3N2) virus infection in two children--Indiana and Pennsylvania, July-August 2011.
reason: Reports two children infected with swine-origin influenza A(H3N2) reassortants carrying the pdm09 M gene, with exposure to swine: a direct report of a new pig-origin influenza A virus appearing in people.

title: Los virus Influenza y la nueva pandemia A/H1N1
reason: Spanish-language review of influenza viruses and the new pandemic A/H1N1, tracing its triple-reassortant plus Eurasian swine ancestry and its re-emergence in humans, so it covers much of what was asked.

title: Envelope Proteins Pertain with Evolution and Adaptive Mechanism of the Novel Influenza A/H1N1 in Humans
reason: Phylogenetic and mutational analysis of HA and NA showing the novel swine-origin H1N1 arose by reassortment from different lineages and acquired mutations enabling adaptation in humans.

title: Swine Flu (S-OIV) Pandemic
reason: Broad review of the swine-origin H1N1 pandemic that explains the pig mixing-cauldron reassortment and the strain's transmission to and among humans, alongside much material on immunity, epitopes and vaccines.

title: Genetic analysis and antigenic characterization of swine origin influenza viruses isolated from humans in the United States, 1990–2010
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title states genetic and antigenic characterization of swine-origin influenza viruses isolated from humans in the US over 1990-2010, i.e. pig-origin viruses recovered from people.

title: Monoclonal antibodies isolated from human B cells neutralize a broad range of H1 subtype influenza A viruses including swine-origin Influenza virus (S-OIV).
reason: Isolates human monoclonal antibody Fab fragments that neutralize H1 subtype viruses including swine-origin H1N1, aimed at prophylaxis and therapy; the subject is antibody neutralization, not emergence.

title: Isolation and genetic analysis of human origin H1N1 and H3N2 influenza viruses from pigs in China
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title describes isolation of human-origin H1N1 and H3N2 viruses from pigs in China, the human-to-swine direction rather than a pig virus appearing in people.

title: Emergence of a novel swine-origin influenza A (H1N1) virus in humans.
reason: Reports the identification of the novel swine-origin influenza A(H1N1) virus in the first US patients and 642 confirmed human infections, noting its previously unseen genome composition: exactly the question asked.

title: Molecular cloning of the first human monoclonal antibodies neutralizing with high potency swine-origin influenza A pandemic virus (S-OIV).
reason: Molecular cloning of human monoclonal antibodies that potently neutralize the pandemic swine-origin H1N1 for prophylaxis and treatment; a therapeutic antibody paper on the same virus.

title: Birds, Pigs, and People: The Rise of Pandemic Flus
journal: Island Press/Center for Resource Economics eBooks
reason: Chapter on how pandemic flus arise from birds and pigs, opening with the April 2009 San Diego child whose throat swab revealed the new virus; covers the emergence narrative but as a general account.

title: Pathogenesis and transmission of the novel swine-origin influenza virus A/H1N1 after experimental infection of pigs
reason: Experimental intranasal infection of pigs with the pandemic A/H1N1 to measure shedding, clinical signs, T-cell responses and pig-to-pig transmission; pathogenesis in swine, not appearance in humans.

title: An update on swine-origin influenza virus A/H1N1: a review.
reason: Review of the swine-origin A/H1N1 that describes its novel gene constellation, probable origin by reassortment of two swine viruses and its spread from North America worldwide, plus virulence markers and vaccines.

title: The Influenza Pandemic of 2009
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title indicates an account of the 2009 influenza pandemic, which was caused by the new swine-origin H1N1 virus in humans, but the specific focus cannot be confirmed.

title: Introduction of Virulence Markers in PB2 of Pandemic Swine-Origin Influenza Virus Does Not Result in Enhanced Virulence or Transmission
reason: Reverse-genetics test of PB2 virulence markers E627K, D701N and E677G in the pandemic swine-origin virus, assessing replication, pathogenesis and ferret transmission; a virulence determinant question.

title: Novel swine-origin influenza A virus in humans: another pandemic knocking at the door.
reason: Review titled on the novel swine-origin influenza A virus in humans, describing its April 2009 identification in Mexico, its triple-reassortant swine ancestry and its ready human-to-human transmission.

title: Origins and Evolutionary Genomics of the Novel Swine-Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Virus in Humans —Past and Present Perspectives
reason: Directly on the origins and evolutionary genomics of the novel swine-origin A(H1N1) in humans, detailing the six triple-reassortant swine segments plus Eurasian swine NA and M and the timescale of emergence.

title: Chest Radiographic and CT Findings in Novel Swine-Origin Influenza A (H1N1) Virus (S-OIV) Infection
reason: Reviews chest radiograph and CT patterns in patients with swine-origin H1N1 infection including pulmonary embolism in ICU cases; imaging findings are a different question about the same virus.

title: Divergent Human-Origin Influenza Viruses Detected in Australian Swine Populations
reason: Finds that Australian swine influenza diversity was generated exclusively by introductions of human H1N1pdm09 and H3N2 viruses into pigs, the reverse of a pig virus appearing in people.

title: IL-17 response mediates acute lung injury induced by the 2009 Pandemic Influenza A (H1N1) Virus
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title concerns IL-17-mediated acute lung injury caused by the 2009 pandemic H1N1, an immunopathology mechanism question about the same virus.

title: Development and Evaluation of Reverse Transcription Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Assay for Rapid and Real-Time Detection of the Swine-Origin Influenza A H1N1 Virus
reason: No abstract; graded on title alone. Title describes development of an RT-LAMP assay for rapid real-time detection of swine-origin influenza A H1N1, a diagnostic method rather than an emergence study.

title: Emergence of a novel swine-origin influenza A virus (S-OIV) H1N1 virus in humans.
reason: Explicitly on the emergence of the novel swine-origin H1N1 in humans: novel gene constellation from swine reassortment, contrast with earlier non-sustained swine zoonoses, and sustained human-to-human spread.

title: Initial incursion of pandemic (H1N1) 2009 influenza A virus into European pigs
reason: Documents the first detection of pandemic H1N1 2009 in European pigs in Northern Ireland, concluding the herds were infected from humans; the transmission direction is opposite to the question.

title: Yeast complementation reveals a role for an Arabidopsis thaliana late embryogenesis abundant (LEA)-like protein in oxidative stress tolerance.
reason: Subject is AtLEA5 function in oxidative stress tolerance via yeast complementation; drought-sensitive photosynthesis in overexpressors is only a side observation, no inference of metabolic relationships from photosynthesis data.

title: Limitations to leaf photosynthesis in field-grown grapevine under drought — metabolic and modelling approaches
reason: Directly addresses the question: drought-stressed grapevine gas-exchange data are modelled for Rubisco carboxylation, RuBP regeneration and triose-P use, then cross-checked against in vitro enzyme activities, concluding modelling of photosynthesis data can predict metabolic limitations.

title: Integration of crop growth model and constraint-based metabolic model predicts metabolic changes over rice plant development under water-limited stress
reason: Constraint-based genome-scale plus crop growth model predicts metabolic changes, including reduced photosynthesis, under water-limited stress in rice; supplies a real part of the answer that metabolic relationships can be inferred computationally, though not from compiled photosynthesis datasets.

title: Over-expression of a Zea mays L. protein phosphatase 2C gene (ZmPP2C) in Arabidopsis thaliana decreases tolerance to salt and drought.
reason: ZmPP2C overexpression phenotyping for salt and drought tolerance; net photosynthesis is only one stress phenotype among MDA, proline and gene expression, so it is background rather than metabolic inference from photosynthesis data.

title: Stomatal and non-stomatal limitations of photosynthesis for four tree species under drought: A comparison of model formulations
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: comparison of model formulations for stomatal versus non-stomatal (biochemical) limitation of photosynthesis in trees under drought is a real part of inferring metabolic limitation from photosynthesis data.

title: Photosynthetic limitations in response to water stress and recovery in Mediterranean plants with different growth forms
reason: Quantitative limitation analysis partitions water-stress effects on photosynthesis into stomatal, mesophyll conductance and biochemical components across ten Mediterranean species, giving a substantial part of the metabolic-versus-diffusive answer without exploring metabolite-level relationships.

title: Photosynthesis and drought: can we make metabolic connections from available data?
reason: Exactly the question asked: a meta-analysis of over 450 published papers testing whether metabolic connections (sugars, ROS, hormones, ABI1/ABI3) can be drawn from available data on photosynthesis under water deficit, and reporting how fragmented and non-comparable those data are.

title: Metabolic interactions in leaf development in Arabidopsis thaliana
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: metabolic interactions in Arabidopsis leaf development concern developmental metabolism, not photosynthesis under water limitation.

title: Arabidopsis ABA Response Gene ABI1 : Features of a Calcium-Modulated Protein Phosphatase
reason: Cloning and characterisation of ABI1 as a calcium-modulated protein phosphatase in ABA signalling; useful drought-signalling background but contains no photosynthesis measurements or metabolic inference.

title: Cloning and characterization of ChiMYB in Chrysanthemum indicum with an emphasis on salinity stress tolerance.
reason: ChiMYB transcription factor characterised mainly for salinity tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis; photosynthetic rate and drought tolerance appear only as phenotype readouts, not as data for metabolic inference.

title: ABA is required for the accumulation of APX1 and MBF1c during a combination of water deficit and heat stress
reason: Studies APX1 and MBF1c protein accumulation and stomatal aperture in abi1-1 and aba1-1 under combined water deficit and heat; water-limitation context but the readouts are stress proteins and H2O2, not photosynthetic metabolism.

title: Interactive effects of drought and pathogens in forest trees
reason: Review of drought-disease interactions in forest trees, focused on pathogen predisposition and fungal biology; shares the drought context but addresses pathology, with no photosynthesis or metabolite data.

title: ABI2, a second protein phosphatase 2C involved in abscisic acid signal transduction in Arabidopsis
reason: Identification of ABI2 as a second PP2C in ABA signal transduction, assessed through germination and phosphatase activity; molecular signalling background only, no photosynthesis or metabolic relationships.

title: Abscisic acid affects transcription of chloroplast genes via protein phosphatase 2C-dependent activation of nuclear genes: repression by guanosine-3'-5'-bisdiphosphate and activation by sigma factor 5.
journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
reason: Shows ABA represses chloroplast gene transcription via PP2C-dependent nuclear genes, ppGpp and SIG5; touches photosynthetic gene regulation but no water-deficit treatment and no metabolic inference from photosynthesis data.

title: Variation in photosynthetic characteristics with growth form in a water-limited scenario: Implications for assimilation rates and water use efficiency in crops
reason: Compiles available photosynthesis data across growth forms to elucidate mesophyll-diffusion versus biochemical limitations under water stress, so it reuses existing photosynthesis data for a water-limited scenario, but the focus is limitation partitioning and water use efficiency rather than metabolic relationships.

title: ABA receptor PYL9 promotes drought resistance and leaf senescence
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: PYL9 overexpression promoting drought resistance and ABA-induced leaf senescence via SnRK2s, ABFs and RAV1; drought-response biology but no photosynthetic or metabolic data to infer relationships from.

title: Function of ABA in Stomatal Defense against Biotic and Drought Stresses
reason: Review of ABA signal components (PYR/PYL/RCAR, PP2C, SnRK2) in stomatal defence against biotic and drought stress; signalling background for water limitation, no photosynthesis metabolism analysis.

title: Methods and concepts in quantifying resistance to drought, salt and freezing, abiotic stresses that affect plant water status
reason: Methods paper on quantifying drought, salt and freezing resistance using PEG plates, root elongation and electrolyte leakage; same water-potential stress field but it supplies assay protocols, not photosynthesis or metabolic relationships.

title: Causes of decreased photosynthetic rate and metabolic capacity in water-deficient leaf cells: a critical evaluation of mechanisms and integration of processes
reason: Critically evaluates existing evidence on stomatal conductance versus photosynthetic metabolic potential in water-deficient leaves, integrating ATP, RuBP, Rubisco, photorespiration and ROS results into a qualitative model of photosynthetic metabolism under water deficit, exactly the inference the question asks about.

title: Relationships of Leaf Net Photosynthesis, Stomatal Conductance, and Mesophyll Conductance to Primary Metabolism: A Multispecies Meta-Analysis Approach
reason: Multispecies meta-analysis of 17 published studies deriving statistical relationships between net photosynthesis, gs, gm and primary metabolites, so it demonstrates metabolic relationships can be inferred from existing photosynthesis data, but the compiled data are not specifically water-limitation experiments.

title: A balancing act: how plants integrate nitrogen and water signals
reason: Reviews how nitrogen and water signals interact via root architecture, stomatal aperture and transcriptomic meta-analysis; concerns water status signalling and N metabolism genes rather than metabolic limitation of photosynthesis.

title: The metabolic response to drought
reason: Reviews existing metabolite profiling data to define the specific metabolic signature of water-deficit stress in Arabidopsis and rice, which supplies a real part of the answer on metabolic responses under water limitation, though photosynthesis is not the analysed variable.

title: Keeping a positive carbon balance under adverse conditions: responses of photosynthesis and respiration to water stress
reason: Synthesises published photosynthesis and respiration data under water stress to establish gs thresholds at which diffusive limitation gives way to photochemical and biochemical failure, and argues metabolic responses arise indirectly through oxidative stress; that is metabolic relationships drawn from existing photosynthesis data.

title: Early PLDalpha-mediated events in response to progressive drought stress in Arabidopsis: a transcriptome analysis.
reason: Transcriptome analysis of antisense-PLDalpha Arabidopsis under progressive drought, with leaf water potential and photosynthesis as physiological framing; the inferred relationships are gene expression, not metabolic, so it is background only.

title: The oil palm R2R3-MYB subfamily genes EgMYB111 and EgMYB157 improve multiple abiotic stress tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis plants.
reason: Overexpression of oil palm EgMYB111 and EgMYB157 for cold, salt and drought tolerance; photosynthetic rate and stomatal conductance are phenotype readouts in a gene-function study, not data used to infer metabolic relationships.

title: Modelling C3 and C4 photosynthesis under water-stressed conditions
reason: No abstract available, graded on title alone: modelling C3 and C4 photosynthesis under water-stressed conditions is directly about deriving photosynthetic parameters, including biochemical ones, for water-limited conditions.

title: Drought stress and reactive oxygen species
reason: Reviews ROS production in chloroplasts, peroxisomes and mitochondria and antioxidant/ABA signalling under drought; relevant drought context but centred on redox signalling rather than photosynthetic metabolic relationships.

title: Flux Balance Analysis of Photoautotrophic Metabolism
reason: Flux balance analysis of photoautotrophic metabolism in Synechocystis with photophosphorylation coupling; same modelling technique applied to a different problem, since no water limitation is considered.
